ca462-lathrop-born-of-a-quarrel.a: Lathrop did not become a city until 1989. Today large planned neighborhoods, among them River Islands, spread west of the freeway.
ca462-lathrop-born-of-a-quarrel.quote: Lathrop did not become a city until 1989. Today large planned neighborhoods, among them River Islands, spread west of the freeway.

ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.q: Why was Flying Scotsman hidden near Roth Road?
alts: Why was it hidden at that Army depot?
Why was a train hiding here?
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.a: Its owner had gone bankrupt touring it across North America, so he stored the engine at the Army depot here, out of reach of his creditors.
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.quote: he stored the engine at the Army depot here, out of reach of his creditors

ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.q: What was the Flying Scotsman famous for?
alts: What was special about that train, mister?
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.a: It's often called the world's most famous steam locomotive. It was the first steam locomotive officially clocked at 100 miles per hour.
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.quote: the first steam locomotive officially clocked at 100 miles per hour

ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.q: How old is the Flying Scotsman?
alts: How old is that train, anyway?
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.a: It was built in 1923. It retired from regular service in 1963 after running more than 2 million miles.
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.quote: Built in 1923, Flying Scotsman was the first steam locomotive officially clocked at 100 miles per hour

ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.q: Who owned the Flying Scotsman when it came to America?
alts: Whose train was it, and why did he bring it?
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.a: Businessman Alan Pegler bought it. With support from the British government, he toured it through the United States and Canada from 1969 to promote British exports.
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.quote: Businessman Alan Pegler bought it and, with support from the British government, sent it touring the United States and Canada from 1969

ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.q: Why did the Flying Scotsman tour run into trouble in America?
alts: What went wrong with it on the tour?
Why did the train get in trouble, mom?
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.a: Some states treated the steam engine as a fire hazard. The tour ran 15,400 miles, but in 1972 Pegler, deep in debt, declared bankruptcy.
ca465-flying-scotsman-in-hiding.quote: some states treated the steam engine as a fire hazard, and in 1972 Pegler, deep in debt, declared bankruptcy

alts: Who stayed at it every year?
Who lived here, like way back?
ca467-french-camp.a: French Canadian trappers working for the Hudson's Bay Company camped here every year with their families, from about 1832 to 1845.
ca467-french-camp.quote: From about 1832 to 1845, French Canadian trappers working for the Hudson's Bay Company camped here every year with their families.

alts: Is French Camp like super old?
ca467-french-camp.a: French Camp is considered the oldest settlement in San Joaquin County.
ca467-french-camp.quote: French Camp is considered the oldest settlement in San Joaquin County.

ca467-french-camp.q: What did the trappers do at French Camp?
alts: What were they doing at it?
What were the trappers hunting for, anyway?
ca467-french-camp.a: They were fur trappers working for the Hudson's Bay Company. It was the southernmost regular camp of fur brigades sent all the way from Fort Vancouver.
ca467-french-camp.quote: It was the southernmost regular camp of fur brigades sent all the way from Fort Vancouver, in what is now Vancouver, Washington.

ca467-french-camp.q: What is at French Camp today?
ca467-french-camp.a: Today French Camp is home to the county hospital and an Army depot.
ca467-french-camp.quote: Today French Camp is home to the county hospital and an Army depot.

ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.q: When did the first Sikh temple in America open?
alts: How old is that temple, like really old?
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.a: Gurdwara Sahib Stockton opened on October 24, 1912, in a house. It was the first Sikh house of worship in the United States.
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.quote: Gurdwara Sahib Stockton opened on October 24, 1912, in a house.

ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.q: Who founded the first Sikh temple in America?
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.a: Its founders were Punjabi Sikh immigrants who farmed the land around Stockton. One founder was Jawala Singh, a successful potato farmer.
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.quote: Its founders were Punjabi Sikh immigrants who farmed the land around Stockton.

ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.a: Jawala Singh was a successful potato farmer who worked a 500-acre ranch next to Stockton with his partner Wasakha Singh. He later helped form the Ghadar Party.
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.quote: One founder, Jawala Singh, was a successful potato farmer who worked a 500-acre ranch next to Stockton with his partner Wasakha Singh.

ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.q: Where did the Sikh farmers first pray before the temple?
alts: Where did they pray at first?
Where did they meet before it was built?
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.a: Sikh farmers newly arrived from Punjab first gathered to pray in a room on Jawala Singh's ranch.
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.quote: Sikh farmers newly arrived from Punjab first gathered to pray in a room on that ranch.

ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.q: Who got help from the first Sikh temple in America?
alts: Did a famous person come from it?
Who did it help go to college?
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.a: The gurdwara paid for the university studies of Dalip Singh Saund. He later became the first Sikh American and the first Asian American elected to Congress.
ca470-first-sikh-temple-in-america.quote: The gurdwara also paid for the university studies of Dalip Singh Saund, who later became the first Sikh American and the first Asian American elected to Congress.

ca472-little-manila.q: What was Little Manila in Stockton?
ca472-little-manila.a: It was a downtown Stockton neighborhood south of Main Street. By 1946 it held the largest Filipino community in the United States.
ca472-little-manila.quote: By 1946 this downtown neighborhood, south of Main Street, held the largest Filipino community in the United States.

ca472-little-manila.q: Why did Filipino men build their own community in Stockton?
alts: Why couldn't they just live in town?
ca472-little-manila.a: Racist laws kept most of them from marrying, and they were barred from crossing Main Street into the white north side. So they built their own community with hotels, barber shops, restaurants and social clubs.
ca472-little-manila.quote: So they built their own community, with hotels, barber shops, restaurants and social clubs.

ca472-little-manila.q: What happened to Little Manila when the freeway came?
ca472-little-manila.a: The Crosstown Freeway was built in the early 1970s through part of it. Residents fought the freeway and lost, and it displaced many Filipino homes and businesses.
ca472-little-manila.quote: Residents fought the freeway and lost, and it displaced many Filipino homes and businesses.

ca472-little-manila.q: What is the Filipino Plaza near Little Manila?
ca472-little-manila.a: The community raised money to build it, and it was completed in 1972. It became home to displaced families and to the Barrio Fiesta, a Filipino cultural festival held each August.
ca472-little-manila.quote: The community raised money to build the Filipino Plaza, completed in 1972, which became home to displaced families

alts: Is there a real guy named Stockton?
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.a: It was named for Commodore Robert Stockton, a famed naval commander of the Mexican-American War.
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.quote: He soon renamed it for Commodore Robert Stockton, a famed naval commander of the Mexican-American War.

ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.q: What is Stockton famous for in California history?
alts: What is it known for historically?
Why is this town special, like what's the big deal?
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.a: It was the first town in California with a name that was neither Spanish nor Native American. It also boomed as a supply stop for gold miners.
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.quote: That made Stockton the first town in California with a name that was neither Spanish nor Native American.

ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.q: Why did Stockton grow during the Gold Rush?
alts: Why did it boom for gold miners?
Why did the miners go there, like what was it for?
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.a: As the head of navigation on the San Joaquin River, Stockton boomed as a supply stop for gold miners.
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.quote: As the head of navigation on the San Joaquin River, it boomed as a supply stop for gold miners.

ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.q: Who lived in the Stockton area before the town?
alts: Were there Native Americans there, kids want to know?
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.a: This is the homeland of the Yatchicumne, a branch of the Northern Valley Yokuts. They built their villages on low mounds to stay above the regular floods.
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.quote: This is the homeland of the Yatchicumne, a branch of the Northern Valley Yokuts, who built their villages on low mounds to stay above the regular floods.

ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.q: Did Stockton have any other nicknames?
alts: Did it go by other names too?
Were there funny names for it?
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.a: Yes. In its early years Stockton also went by Weberville, Fat City and Mudville. It's also one of a handful of cities claiming to have inspired the poem Casey at the Bat.
ca472-stockton-once-tuleburg.quote: In its early years Stockton also went by Weberville, Fat City and Mudville, and it is one of a handful of cities that claim to have inspired the 1888 poem Casey at the Bat.

ca473-port-of-stockton.q: How can Stockton be a seaport if it's so far inland?
alts: How do ocean ships even get up to it?
How do big boats get all the way to Stockton?
ca473-port-of-stockton.a: Ocean ships come up a dredged channel, 35 feet deep, from San Francisco Bay. Ships up to 900 feet long can make the trip to the docks.
ca473-port-of-stockton.quote: Ocean ships up to 900 feet long come up a dredged channel, 35 feet deep, from San Francisco Bay.

ca473-port-of-stockton.q: When did the Port of Stockton open?
alts: How long has that been here?
ca473-port-of-stockton.a: The modern port opened on February 2, 1933, when the ship Daisy Grey arrived with a load of lumber from Oregon.
ca473-port-of-stockton.quote: The modern port opened on February 2, 1933, when the ship Daisy Grey arrived with a load of lumber from Oregon.

ca473-port-of-stockton.q: What was the Port of Stockton used for in the Gold Rush?
alts: What did it do back then?
Why were boats coming here for gold?
ca473-port-of-stockton.a: The San Joaquin River was deep enough for ocean-going vessels, so Stockton became a natural supply point for miners. The first freight vessel, the sloop Maria, called here in 1848.
ca473-port-of-stockton.quote: During the Gold Rush the San Joaquin River was deep enough for ocean-going vessels, which made Stockton a natural supply point for miners.

ca473-port-of-stockton.q: What happened at the Port of Stockton in World War Two?
alts: What did it do in the war?
ca473-port-of-stockton.a: The War Department wanted ships built at an inland port, safe from attack on the coast. So many new ships were built here.
ca473-port-of-stockton.quote: During World War Two the War Department wanted ships built at an inland port, safe from attack on the coast, so many new ships were built here.

ca473-port-of-stockton.q: How big is the Port of Stockton?
alts: How much land does that cover?
ca473-port-of-stockton.a: By land area it is the second largest port in California, covering about 4,200 acres.
ca473-port-of-stockton.quote: By land area it is the second largest port in California, covering about 4,200 acres.

ca473-port-of-stockton.q: What is the Navy supply depot on Rough and Ready Island?
alts: Did the Navy have a base here?
ca473-port-of-stockton.a: It was a major communications post for submarines in the Pacific during the Cold War. It is now the port's West Complex.
ca473-port-of-stockton.quote: The Navy's supply depot on Rough and Ready Island, a major communications post for submarines in the Pacific during the Cold War, is now the port's West Complex.

ca474-university-of-the-pacific.q: How old is the University of the Pacific?
alts: Is that school really old, like how many years?
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.a: It was chartered in 1851, which made it the first university chartered in California. It started out in Santa Clara before it ever came to Stockton.
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.quote: It was the first university chartered in California, in 1851, and it started out in Santa Clara.

ca474-university-of-the-pacific.q: Where was the University of the Pacific before Stockton?
alts: Did it always stay in the same place?
Did the school move around, like to other towns?
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.a: It started out in Santa Clara, moved to San Jose in 1871, and then moved to Stockton in 1924.
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.quote: It moved to San Jose in 1871 and to Stockton in 1924.

ca474-university-of-the-pacific.q: What is the University of the Pacific famous for?
alts: What's so special about that school?
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.a: It's known for firsts. Pacific opened the first medical school on the West Coast in 1858, and its music conservatory, founded in 1878, was the first of its kind west of the Mississippi.
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.quote: Pacific also opened the first medical school on the West Coast, in 1858.

ca474-university-of-the-pacific.q: Did anyone famous go to the University of the Pacific?
alts: Did a famous person study there?
Did anybody cool go to that school?
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.a: Yes, the pianist and composer Dave Brubeck graduated from Pacific in 1942.
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.quote: the pianist and composer Dave Brubeck graduated from Pacific in 1942.

ca474-university-of-the-pacific.q: Has Hollywood filmed at the University of the Pacific?
alts: Did they shoot a movie at that campus?
Is it in Raiders of the Lost Ark?
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.a: Yes, Hollywood has filmed here many times, including scenes for Raiders of the Lost Ark. The brick buildings, tower and rose gardens look like an old East Coast college.
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.quote: Hollywood has filmed here many times, including scenes for Raiders of the Lost Ark.

ca474-university-of-the-pacific.q: What can you see on the University of the Pacific campus?
alts: Is there anything cool to see on that campus?
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.a: You'll see brick buildings, a tower and rose gardens, and the Calaveras River flows through the campus.
ca474-university-of-the-pacific.quote: The Calaveras River flows through the campus.

ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.q: Why is it called the Calaveras River?
alts: Why's the river named after skulls?
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.a: Calaveras is Spanish for skulls. The river is said to have been named in 1806 by the Spanish explorer Gabriel Moraga, when he found many skulls of Native people along its banks.
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.quote: Calaveras is Spanish for skulls. The river is said to have been named in 1806 by the Spanish explorer Gabriel Moraga, when he found many skulls of Native people along its banks.

alts: Who got to name the skull river?
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.a: Spanish explorer Gabriel Moraga is said to have named it in 1806. Another story says an 1836 party that included John Marsh and José Noriega gave it the same name.
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.quote: Another story says an 1836 party that included John Marsh and José Noriega camped along the river one evening and woke to find skulls and bones all around them

ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.q: What happened to the people whose skulls were found there?
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.a: Moraga believed the people had died of famine or in fights over hunting and fishing grounds. That is his belief, as the source tells it, not a proven fact.
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.quote: Moraga believed the people had died of famine or in fights over hunting and fishing grounds.

ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.q: How long is the Calaveras River?
alts: How big is the skull river?
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.a: It runs about 52 miles, from Calaveras County to the San Joaquin River, with just one reservoir along the way, New Hogan Lake.
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.quote: The Calaveras runs about 52 miles from Calaveras County to the San Joaquin River, with just one reservoir along the way, New Hogan Lake.

ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.q: What does the Calaveras River have to do with Stockton?
alts: What does it do around Stockton?
Does the river go around the city?
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.a: The river and its side channel, Mormon Slough, wrap around central Stockton, so much of the city is really one of the many islands of the Delta.
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.quote: It and its side channel, Mormon Slough, wrap around central Stockton, so much of the city is really one of the many islands of the Delta.

ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.q: Which exit is the Calaveras River?
alts: What exit do we take for the skull river?
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.a: The freeway crosses the Calaveras River here, at exit 476.
ca476-calaveras-river-river-of-skulls.quote: The freeway crosses the Calaveras River here.

alts: Who's this Holt guy the exit is named after?
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.a: Benjamin Holt was a Stockton inventor. He came to Stockton in 1883 and, with his brothers, started a company making wagon wheels, then combine harvesters and tractors.
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.quote: Holt came to Stockton in 1883 and, with his brothers, started a company that made wagon wheels, then combine harvesters and tractors.

ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.q: How did the Caterpillar get its name?
alts: Why is a tractor called a caterpillar?
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.a: A company photographer was reported to have said Holt's tracked tractor crawled like a caterpillar. Holt liked it and said, "Caterpillar it is."
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.quote: A company photographer was reported to have said it crawled like a caterpillar. Holt liked it: Caterpillar it is, he said

ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.q: When did Holt first test the Caterpillar tractor?
alts: When did the tractor first roll, kids want to know?
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.a: Holt tested it on Thanksgiving Day, November 24, 1904. The tractor rode on tracks instead of wheels and plowed soggy Delta farmland near Stockton.
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.quote: On Thanksgiving Day, November 24, 1904, Holt tested a tractor that rode on tracks instead of wheels, plowing soggy Delta farmland near Stockton.

ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.q: Why did Holt put tracks on a tractor?
alts: Why not just use wheels like a normal tractor?
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.a: Most fields around Stockton were reclaimed from the Delta, so the ground was soft. Tracks spread a heavy machine's weight so it would not sink.
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.quote: tracks spread a heavy machine's weight so it would not sink into the soft ground.

ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.q: What did Holt's company do in World War One?
alts: Was it used in the war?
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.a: During World War One, Allied armies used about 10,000 Holt vehicles, many of them hauling heavy guns.
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.quote: During World War One, Allied armies used about 10,000 Holt vehicles, many of them hauling heavy guns.

ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.q: Can we see a Holt Caterpillar tractor today?
alts: Can we see an old one somewhere?
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.a: Yes, a restored Holt Caterpillar tractor from around 1918 is on display at the Haggin Museum in Stockton.
ca477-benjamin-holt-and-the-caterpillar.quote: A restored Holt Caterpillar tractor from around 1918 is on display at the Haggin Museum in Stockton.

ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.q: What was the last piece of I-5 to open?
alts: What was it that finished last?
What part of the freeway was built last, mom?
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.a: A 4.6-mile stretch of freeway north of Stockton was the very last piece of Interstate 5 to open.
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.quote: A 4.6-mile stretch of freeway north of Stockton was the very last piece of Interstate 5 to open.

ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.q: When did the last piece of I-5 open?
alts: When was the freeway finally done, dad?
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.a: It opened on October 12, 1979, after 26 years of construction, completing I-5 from the Mexican border to the Canadian border.
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.quote: On October 12, 1979, after 26 years of construction, the consuls of Canada and Mexico joined California's transportation secretary to cut a gold-colored chain

ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.q: How long did it take to build all of I-5?
alts: How long did it take to finish it?
Did it take a really long time to make this road?
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.a: Construction took 26 years, ending in 1979 when the last piece opened and I-5 was complete from Mexico to Canada.
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.quote: On October 12, 1979, after 26 years of construction, the consuls of Canada and Mexico joined California's transportation secretary to cut a gold-colored chain

ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.q: Who was at the last piece of I-5 opening ceremony?
alts: Who was there when it opened?
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.a: The consuls of Canada and Mexico joined California's transportation secretary to cut a gold-colored chain, finishing I-5 from border to border.
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.quote: the consuls of Canada and Mexico joined California's transportation secretary to cut a gold-colored chain, completing Interstate 5 from the Mexican border to the Canadian border.

ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.q: What exit is the last piece of I-5?
alts: Which exit do we look for, dad?
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.a: It's exit 481, on the stretch of freeway north of Stockton.
ca481-the-last-piece-of-i-5.quote: A 4.6-mile stretch of freeway north of Stockton was the very last piece of Interstate 5 to open.

alts: Why do people come to Lodi, mom?
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.a: Lodi is a town surrounded by vineyards, and it's the birthplace of A&W Root Beer. It also once called itself the Tokay Capital of the World.
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.quote: Lodi is also the birthplace of A&W Root Beer: in 1919 Roy Allen sold his first batch from a cart during a parade

ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.q: Why is the town called Lodi?
alts: How did it get that name?
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.a: Nobody is sure why Lodi was chosen. Most likely some early settlers came from a place called Lodi in Illinois. It was first called Mokelumne, but that caused confusion with other towns.
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.quote: Nobody is sure why Lodi was chosen. One story credits a record-setting local trotting horse

alts: Are there lots of grapes, dad?
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.a: Lodi's growers raise more than 130 grape varieties. Many of the old vines were planted between the Gold Rush and Prohibition. It was also known for Flame Tokay grapes.
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.quote: Its growers raise more than 130 grape varieties, and many of the old vines here were planted between the Gold Rush and Prohibition.

ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.q: Is there a song about Lodi?
alts: Is there a song named Lodi, mom?
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.a: Yes, Creedence Clearwater Revival has a song called Lodi. John Fogerty admits he had never been here and just thought it was the coolest sounding name.
ca485-lodi-wine-and-root-beer.quote: The Creedence Clearwater Revival song Lodi is named for this town, although songwriter John Fogerty admits he had never been here

ca487-delta-asparagus.q: When did asparagus first get grown in the Delta?
alts: When did they start growing it?
When did kids' favorite veggie farming start here?
ca487-delta-asparagus.a: The first commercial crop was grown in 1892 on Bouldin Island. Chinese farmers planted it, and by about 1900 it was becoming a signature crop of the Delta.
ca487-delta-asparagus.quote: The first commercial crop was grown in 1892 on Bouldin Island by Chinese farmers.

ca487-delta-asparagus.q: How did they harvest Delta asparagus?
alts: How did they cut the spears, anyway?
ca487-delta-asparagus.a: Every spear was cut by hand. Workers slipped a long knife just below the surface of the sticky peat soil, and crews walked each field every few days during the spring harvest.
ca487-delta-asparagus.quote: Every spear was cut by hand, with a long knife slipped just below the surface of the sticky peat soil

ca487-delta-asparagus.q: Who worked the Delta asparagus fields?
ca487-delta-asparagus.a: Chinese immigrants did the first hand labor, followed by Japanese workers, then Filipinos, and later Mexican workers. In 1930, 5,500 of about 7,000 harvest workers were Filipino.
ca487-delta-asparagus.quote: Chinese immigrants did the first hand labor, followed by Japanese workers, then Filipinos, and later Mexican workers.

ca487-delta-asparagus.a: Thomas Foon Chew was known as the Asparagus King. In 1919 he moved his Bayside Cannery to Isleton, and at its peak it was the third-largest canning company in the country.
ca487-delta-asparagus.quote: In 1919 Thomas Foon Chew, known as the Asparagus King, moved his Bayside Cannery to Isleton, on the Sacramento River

ca487-delta-asparagus.q: Is Delta asparagus still a big crop today?
alts: Is it still a thing, or did it go away?
ca487-delta-asparagus.a: Not like it used to be. By the mid-1980s, competition from lower-wage countries such as Peru and Mexico had shrunk the crop, and fresh Delta asparagus has become hard to find.
ca487-delta-asparagus.quote: By the mid-1980s, competition from lower-wage countries such as Peru and Mexico had shrunk the crop, and fresh Delta asparagus has become hard to find.

ca487-delta-asparagus.q: How big was the Delta asparagus business back then?
alts: Were there lots of workers or just a few?
ca487-delta-asparagus.a: Pretty big. In 1930 the Delta had more than 350 asparagus camps holding about 7,000 harvest workers.
ca487-delta-asparagus.quote: In 1930 the Delta had more than 350 asparagus camps holding about 7,000 harvest workers, 5,500 of them Filipino.

ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.q: When do the sandhill cranes come to the Sandhill crane reserve?
alts: When do they show up here?
Kid: When do the big birds come?
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.a: They arrive in the Delta around late September and spend the fall and winter here. The best months to see them are October through February.
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.quote: Sandhill cranes arrive in the Delta around late September and spend the fall and winter here.

ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.q: What's the best time of day to watch the cranes at the Sandhill crane reserve?
alts: Kid: When do the birds fly in?
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.a: Sunset is the best time. That's when you can watch them fly in, and they make a loud, trumpeting call you can hear from a long way off.
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.quote: Sunset is the best time to watch them fly in, giving a loud, trumpeting call that can be heard from a long way off.

ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.q: How big are the sandhill cranes at the Sandhill crane reserve?
alts: Kid: Are the birds really huge?
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.a: Their wings spread about six and a half feet, so these are big birds.
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.quote: Their wings spread about six and a half feet.

ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.q: How old are sandhill cranes as a bird?
alts: How long have they been around?
Kid: Were these birds around with dinosaurs?
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.a: Sandhill cranes have one of the longest fossil histories of any living bird. The oldest sure fossil is 2.5 million years old.
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.quote: Sandhill cranes have one of the longest fossil histories of any living bird, and the oldest sure fossil is 2.5 million years old.

alts: Kid: Are the birds in danger?
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.a: California listed the greater sandhill crane as threatened in 1983, after its numbers fell.
ca490-sandhill-crane-reserve.quote: California listed the greater sandhill crane as threatened in 1983, after its numbers fell.

ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.q: Why is the Delta's soil so rich?
alts: Why is it so rich and good for growing?
Why's the dirt there so good, anyway?
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.a: Over thousands of years, tules and reeds grew and decayed there into peat as much as 50 feet deep. That deep peat is why the soil is so rich.
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.quote: Over thousands of years, tules and reeds grew and decayed here into peat as much as 50 feet deep, which is why the soil is so rich.

ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.q: Is the land in the Delta really below sea level?
alts: Is it really that low, below the sea?
Wait, is the ground there lower than the ocean?
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.a: Yes. Much of the western and central Delta sits at least 15 feet below sea level, and the land has sunk as much as 25 feet since the late 1800s.
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.quote: Much of the western and central Delta now sits at least 15 feet below sea level.

ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.q: Why has the land in the Delta sunk so much?
alts: Why did it sink like that?
Why is the ground sinking, Dad?
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.a: Once the marsh was drained, the peat soil met the air and slowly broke down. The land has sunk as much as 25 feet since the late 1800s.
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.quote: Once the marsh was drained, its peat soil met the air and slowly broke down, and the land has sunk as much as 25 feet since the late 1800s.

ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.q: Who built the levees around the Delta?
alts: Who built the walls that hold the water back?
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.a: Chinese laborers did much of the first levee building, from the 1850s to the 1870s. About 1,100 miles of levees now ring the islands and tracts.
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.quote: Chinese laborers did much of the first levee building, from the 1850s to the 1870s.

ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.q: Why is the Delta important for California's water?
alts: Why does it matter so much for water?
Why do people care about the Delta's water?
What's the big deal with its water?
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.a: About half of all the river water in California flows through the Delta. Water pumped from its southern end helps supply some 23 million people.
ca490-the-delta-california-s-holland.quote: About half of all the river water in California flows through the Delta, and water pumped from its southern end helps supply some 23 million people.

alts: Why's it called People of the Fish Net, Mom?
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.a: Mokelumne means People of the Fish Net. It joins the Miwok words moke, a fishnet, and umne, people of.
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.quote: Mokelumne joins moke, a fishnet, with umne, people of, so it means People of the Fish Net.

ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.q: Where does the name Mokelumne come from?
alts: Where does that name come from?
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.a: Both Mokelumne and the nearby Cosumnes come from Miwok. Cosumnes is thought to be built the same way, from kosum, meaning salmon.
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.quote: Both names come from Miwok. Mokelumne joins moke, a fishnet, with umne, people of

ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.q: Who lived along the Mokelumne River long ago?
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.a: This lower river country is thought to be mostly Plains Miwok homeland. Many villages once stood between the Sierra foothills and the edge of the Delta.
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.quote: This lower river country is thought to be mostly Plains Miwok homeland, with many villages once standing between the Sierra foothills and the edge of the Delta.

ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.q: What did the Miwok call the Mokelumne River?
alts: What was it called before that?
What's the river's old name, Mom?
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.a: The Miwok called it Wakalumitch, possibly meaning big river. A Spanish missionary first wrote down the name as Muquelumnes in 1817.
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.quote: The Miwok called the river Wakalumitch, possibly meaning big river. A Spanish missionary first wrote the name down as Muquelumnes in 1817

ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.q: What happens to the Mokelumne River's water?
alts: Does the water go anywhere, Dad?
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.a: Far upstream, Pardee Dam, finished in 1929, feeds the Mokelumne Aqueduct. It carries the river's water across the Delta to the East Bay, the only water supply for about 1.4 million people there.
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.quote: Pardee Dam, finished in 1929, feeds the Mokelumne Aqueduct, which carries the river's water across the Delta to the East Bay.

ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.q: Where does the Mokelumne River go after the freeway?
alts: Where does it go from here?
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.a: Downstream from here, the Mokelumne splits in two around Staten Island before it reaches the San Joaquin.
ca493-mokelumne-people-of-the-fish-net.quote: Downstream from here, the Mokelumne splits in two around Staten Island before it reaches the San Joaquin.

ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.q: How big is the Cosumnes River Preserve?
alts: Is that place really huge, like how many acres?
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.a: It covers nearly 50,000 acres, including some of the largest remaining wetlands and streamside habitat in the Central Valley.
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.quote: covers nearly 50,000 acres, including some of the largest remaining wetlands and streamside habitat in the Central Valley

ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.q: What makes the Cosumnes River special?
alts: Why is the river different from other rivers, mom?
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.a: It's one of very few rivers on the western slope of the Sierra Nevada without a major dam, so it still floods over its banks in season.
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.quote: The Cosumnes is one of very few rivers on the western slope of the Sierra Nevada without a major dam

ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.q: What animals can we see at the Cosumnes River Preserve?
alts: Are there any cool birds there, like big ones?
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.a: Raptors, herons, sandhill cranes, shorebirds and waterfowl all use the preserve. The seasonal flooding makes important habitat for wintering birds.
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.quote: Raptors, herons, sandhill cranes, shorebirds and waterfowl all use it.

ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.q: Why does the Cosumnes River Preserve flood?
alts: Why does the water go over the banks?
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.a: With no major dam, the river still floods over its banks in season. That creates important habitat for wintering birds.
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.quote: so it still floods over its banks in season, creating important habitat for wintering birds.

ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.q: Who runs the Cosumnes River Preserve?
alts: Who's in charge of that place?
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.a: The preserve is managed by a partnership of state, local, federal and private groups. The visitor center is on Franklin Boulevard.
ca498-cosumnes-river-preserve.quote: the preserve is managed by a partnership of state, local, federal and private groups.

alts: Who built it and why did they build it?
Who made this town, kids want to know?
ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.a: Immigrants from Heungshan County, in Guangdong, built it up after a 1915 fire destroyed the Chinese community in Walnut Grove.
ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.quote: Immigrants from Heungshan County, in Guangdong, built it up after a 1915 fire destroyed the Chinese community in Walnut Grove.

ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.q: Why couldn't the people in Locke own their land?
alts: Why did people rent the ground, what was the rule?
ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.a: California's Alien Land Law barred them from owning land. They leased about nine acres and owned only their buildings, and for decades couldn't buy the land under their homes.
ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.quote: California's Alien Land Law barred them from owning land, so they leased about nine acres from George Locke and owned only their buildings.

ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.q: How many people lived in Locke?
alts: Was it a big town with lots of people?
ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.a: At times as many as 1,000 to 1,500 Chinese people lived in Locke, with the numbers swelling during the growing and harvest seasons.
ca498-locke-a-chinese-river-town.quote: At times as many as 1,000 to 1,500 Chinese people lived in Locke, with the numbers swelling during the growing and harvest seasons.

ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.q: What can we do at Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge?
alts: Is there anything for kids to do there?
ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.a: You can walk a mile of paved trail loops around managed wetlands. Kids can use a natural playscape, but there's no visitor center.
ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.quote: The refuge has a mile of paved trail loops around managed wetlands and a natural playscape for children, but no visitor center.

ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.q: Why is Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge important?
alts: Why did they save that land?
ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.a: It protects wild habitat and farmland in an area squeezed by urban growth, between the city of Elk Grove and farm country.
ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.quote: The refuge protects wild habitat and farmland in an area squeezed by urban growth, between the city of Elk Grove and farm country.

ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.q: What is a heron rookery at Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge?
alts: Where do the herons nest there?
What do the birds do there?
ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.a: A rookery is a place where birds nest together in colonies. Stone Lakes holds a major one where great blue herons and other birds nest together.
ca504-stone-lakes-national-wildlife-refu.quote: It holds a major rookery where great blue herons and other birds nest together in colonies.

ca506-elk-grove.q: How did Elk Grove get started?
alts: How'd this town even begin, Dad?
ca506-elk-grove.a: Elk Grove began in 1850 as a stagecoach stop for travelers between Sacramento and the Bay Area, when James Hall opened the Elk Grove Hotel.
ca506-elk-grove.quote: began in 1850 as a stagecoach stop for travelers between Sacramento and the Bay Area, when James Hall opened the Elk Grove Hotel

ca506-elk-grove.q: When did the railroad reach Elk Grove?
alts: When did it get the railroad?
When did the train come here?
ca506-elk-grove.a: The Central Pacific's tracks came through in 1868, about a mile east of the original town. A second Elk Grove Hotel went up near the railroad.
ca506-elk-grove.quote: When the Central Pacific's tracks came through in 1868, about a mile east of the original town, a second Elk Grove Hotel went up near the railroad.

ca506-elk-grove.q: Was Elk Grove always a big suburb?
alts: Was this always a big town?
ca506-elk-grove.a: No. It stayed a small farm town for over a century, until suburbs began spreading in the late 1980s. It became a city on July 1, 2000.
ca506-elk-grove.quote: Elk Grove stayed a small farm town for more than a century, until suburbs began spreading here in the late 1980s, and it did not become a city until July 1, 2000.

ca506-elk-grove.q: How fast has Elk Grove grown?
alts: Is this a fast growing town?
Did a lot of people move here?
ca506-elk-grove.a: In 2004 and 2005 it was declared the fastest growing city in the country. Its population nearly tripled between 2000 and 2020.
ca506-elk-grove.quote: In 2004 and 2005 it was declared the fastest growing city in the country, and its population nearly tripled between 2000 and 2020.

ca506-elk-grove.q: What is Sky River Casino in Elk Grove?
ca506-elk-grove.a: Sky River Casino opened in 2022. The Wilton Rancheria, a federally recognized tribe of Miwok people based in Elk Grove, opened it on the site of a half-built shopping mall.
ca506-elk-grove.quote: In 2022 it opened Sky River Casino in Elk Grove, on the site of a half-built shopping mall.

alts: Why did people even build a town here?
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.a: In 1862, businessmen formed the Freeport Railroad Company to build a new port and a railroad that bypassed Sacramento, so they could dodge Sacramento's port taxes.
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.quote: In 1862, businessmen tired of paying taxes at Sacramento's riverfront landing formed the Freeport Railroad Company

ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.q: How many people live in Freeport?
alts: Is this a big town or a tiny one?
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.a: Very few. The 2020 census counted just 58 people. At its peak, in a three-year boom, the town reached 300 to 400 people.
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.quote: the 2020 census counted just 58 people here

ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.q: What was the plan for the Freeport Railroad?
alts: What was it supposed to do?
Why did they need a railroad?
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.a: It was meant to meet the Sacramento Valley Railroad halfway between Sacramento and Folsom, so freight could skip Sacramento entirely.
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.quote: The plan was for the Freeport Railroad to meet the Sacramento Valley Railroad halfway between Sacramento and Folsom, so freight could skip Sacramento entirely.

ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.q: What is the bridge at Freeport?
alts: What's that bridge over the river?
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.a: Freeport has a drawbridge across the Sacramento River, a bascule bridge. It opened in 1929 and was rebuilt in 1955.
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.quote: Its drawbridge across the river, a bascule bridge, opened in 1929 and was rebuilt in 1955.

ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.q: Where is Freeport on the river?
alts: Which side of the river is it on?
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.a: Freeport sits on the east bank of the Sacramento River, about 7.5 miles south of downtown Sacramento.
ca510-freeport-a-town-born-of-taxes.quote: Freeport sits on the east bank of the Sacramento River about 7.5 miles south of downtown

ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.q: When did the Sacramento Zoo open?
alts: When did the zoo start, mom?
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.a: The zoo opened on June 2, 1927, as the William Land Park Zoo. It started with 40 animals gathered from local parks.
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.quote: The zoo opened on June 2, 1927, as the William Land Park Zoo, with 40 animals gathered from local parks

ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.q: Why is the Sacramento Zoo's elephant named Sue?
alts: Why did they name it Sue?
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.a: Sue stands for Sacramento Union Elephant. Two local sisters named her after the newspaper ran a fund drive in 1948, and she arrived in 1949.
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.quote: Two local sisters named her Sue, for Sacramento Union Elephant.

ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.q: Who was William Land, the man Land Park is named for?
alts: Who is that park named after?
Who was the park guy, dad?
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.a: William Land was a pioneer who built the Western Hotel in 1875. The park around the zoo is named for him.
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.quote: The park around it is named for William Land, a pioneer who built the Western Hotel in 1875.

ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.q: What else is there to do at Land Park besides the zoo?
alts: What else is in the park?
Is there anything for little kids?
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.a: Land Park also holds Fairytale Town, with play equipment based on fairy tales and nursery rhymes. There's also Funderland, with small carnival rides for young children.
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.quote: It also holds Fairytale Town, a park whose play equipment is based on fairy tales and nursery rhymes, and Funderland, with small carnival rides for young children.

ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.q: How big is the Sacramento Zoo and how many animals does it have?
alts: Does the zoo have lots of animals?
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.a: The zoo grew from 4.2 acres to 14.3 acres in the early 1960s. It had just over 500 animals by 2012.
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.quote: The zoo grew from 4.2 acres to 14.3 acres in the early 1960s and had just over 500 animals by 2012.

ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.q: Is the Sacramento Zoo moving somewhere bigger?
alts: Is the zoo getting bigger, dad?
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.a: No. A 2024 plan to move it to Elk Grove was cancelled in April 2025 over cost. The city council approved an expansion where it is.
ca516-sacramento-zoo-and-land-park.quote: A 2024 plan to move it to a bigger site in Elk Grove was cancelled in April 2025 over cost, and the city council approved an expansion where it is.

ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.q: How long has Sacramento been California's capital?
alts: How long has it been the capital?
Has Sacramento always been the capital, Mom?
Since when is it the capital?
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.a: Sacramento has been California's capital since 1854. Before that, lawmakers met in San Jose, then Vallejo in 1852, then Benicia in 1853, before settling here.
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.quote: Sacramento has been California's capital since 1854. The new state's lawmakers first met in San Jose, moved to Vallejo in 1852 and to Benicia in 1853

ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.q: Where did California's capital used to be before Sacramento?
alts: Where was the capital before it moved here?
Did the capital used to be somewhere else, Dad?
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.a: Lawmakers first met in San Jose, moved to Vallejo in 1852 and to Benicia in 1853, and then settled in Sacramento.
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.quote: The new state's lawmakers first met in San Jose, moved to Vallejo in 1852 and to Benicia in 1853, and then settled here.

ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.q: What does the State Capitol in Sacramento look like?
alts: Does the Capitol look like the one in Washington?
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.a: The State Capitol was modeled on the U.S. Capitol. It was begun in 1860 and finished in 1874, and lawmakers moved into its chambers in 1869 while work went on around them.
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.quote: was modeled on the U.S. Capitol. It was begun in 1860 and finished in 1874, and lawmakers moved into its chambers in 1869

ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.q: What is there to see around the Capitol in Sacramento?
alts: What else is there near it?
Are there any parks or trees to see, Mom?
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.a: Capitol Park spreads over 40 acres around the Capitol, with more than 200 kinds of trees and 155 memorials.
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.quote: Capitol Park spreads over 40 acres, with more than 200 kinds of trees and 155 memorials.

ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.q: What was the Pony Express building in Old Sacramento?
alts: What happened at that old brick building?
Did the Pony Express really end here, Dad?
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.a: The B. F. Hastings Building was the western end of the Pony Express in 1860 and 1861. Riders carried mail to and from St. Joseph, Missouri, more than 1,800 miles away.
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.quote: In 1860 and 1861 it was the western end of the Pony Express, whose relays of riders carried mail to and from St. Joseph, Missouri, more than 1,800 miles away.

ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.q: How old is the city of Sacramento?
alts: Is Sacramento a really old city, Mom?
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.a: Sacramento is the oldest incorporated city in California, dating to February 27, 1850.
ca518-sacramento-the-state-capital.quote: Sacramento itself is the oldest incorporated city in California, dating to February 27, 1850.

ca519-tower-bridge.q: How old is the Tower Bridge?
alts: How long has that bridge been here, Dad?
ca519-tower-bridge.a: The Tower Bridge was dedicated in 1935. It replaced an older railroad bridge from 1911.
ca519-tower-bridge.quote: a lift bridge over the Sacramento River dedicated in 1935

ca519-tower-bridge.q: How does the Tower Bridge lift up?
alts: How does the bridge move, Mom?
ca519-tower-bridge.a: Counterweights in the 160-foot towers weigh as much as the 1,150-ton middle span. That balance means just two 100-horsepower electric motors can raise it for tall boats.
ca519-tower-bridge.quote: Its 160-foot towers hold counterweights as heavy as the 1,150-ton middle span, so just two 100-horsepower electric motors can raise it

ca519-tower-bridge.q: Why is the Tower Bridge gold?
alts: Why is the bridge yellow, Dad?
ca519-tower-bridge.a: In 1976 it was painted yellow ochre to match the gold-leafed cupola of the State Capitol. Later, in 2001, residents voted and all gold beat two other color choices.
ca519-tower-bridge.quote: in 1976 it was painted yellow ochre to match the gold-leafed cupola of the nearby State Capitol

ca519-tower-bridge.q: What happened at the Tower Bridge dedication?
alts: What did they do on opening day, Mom?
ca519-tower-bridge.a: A thousand homing pigeons were released to carry the news across California. The dedication was on December 15, 1935.
ca519-tower-bridge.quote: At the dedication on December 15, 1935, a thousand homing pigeons were released to carry the news across California.

ca519-tower-bridge.q: What was here before the Tower Bridge?
ca519-tower-bridge.a: A 1911 railroad bridge stood here first. Trains kept crossing the Tower Bridge until 1962.
ca519-tower-bridge.quote: It replaced a 1911 railroad bridge, and trains crossed it until 1962.

ca519-tower-bridge.q: What else is there to see near the Tower Bridge?
alts: Is there a boat nearby, Mom?
ca519-tower-bridge.a: Just upriver, the Delta King, a 285-foot sternwheel steamboat, is tied up as a hotel. Across the river is the ballpark Sutter Health Park.
ca519-tower-bridge.quote: Just upriver, the Delta King, a 285-foot sternwheel steamboat that ran to San Francisco from 1927 to 1940, is tied up as a hotel.

ca519-the-boat-section.q: When was the Boat Section built?
alts: Is the sunken part really old, Mom?
ca519-the-boat-section.a: It was built in the 1960s and 1970s. The freeway was put below street level on purpose.
ca519-the-boat-section.quote: It was built below street level in the 1960s and 1970s so the freeway would stay out of view of downtown offices and shops

ca519-the-boat-section.q: Why did they build the freeway below street level here?
alts: Why is it sunk down like that?
Why is the road in a hole, Dad?
ca519-the-boat-section.a: So the freeway would stay out of view of downtown offices and shops. Pumps, drains and a retaining wall keep the river's seepage out.
ca519-the-boat-section.quote: so the freeway would stay out of view of downtown offices and shops, and pumps, drains and a retaining wall keep the river's seepage out.

ca519-the-boat-section.q: What happened in Sacramento's Great Flood of 1862?
alts: What was that big flood about?
Did a whole city really go underwater, Dad?
ca519-the-boat-section.a: The American River put much of the city under water for three months. Newly elected governor Leland Stanford had to go to his own inauguration by rowboat.
ca519-the-boat-section.quote: In the Great Flood of 1862 the American River put much of the city under water for three months

ca519-the-boat-section.q: What is Old Sacramento next to the Boat Section?
alts: What's between the freeway and the river?
Is there an old town by the river, Mom?
ca519-the-boat-section.a: Between the freeway and the river lies Old Sacramento, a 28-acre historic district with 53 historic buildings.
ca519-the-boat-section.quote: Between the freeway and the river lies Old Sacramento, a 28-acre historic district with 53 historic buildings.

ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.q: What is inside the California State Railroad Museum?
alts: What can we see in there, Mom?
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.a: It holds 21 restored locomotives and railroad cars, some dating back to 1862. Inside, there's also a big mock-up of railroad construction at Donner Pass around 1867.
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.quote: holds 21 restored locomotives and railroad cars, some dating back to 1862. Inside, a large mock-up recreates railroad construction high in the Sierra at Donner Pass around 1867

ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.q: How old are the trains at the California State Railroad Museum?
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.a: Some of the restored locomotives and cars date back to 1862, and there's also a 1944 steam locomotive, the only surviving Southern Pacific cab-forward.
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.quote: holds 21 restored locomotives and railroad cars, some dating back to 1862

ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.q: What is the Gov. Stanford locomotive at the railroad museum?
alts: Did a train come on a boat?
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.a: It's the Central Pacific's first locomotive. It came to California in pieces by ship, around Cape Horn.
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.quote: the Central Pacific's first locomotive, the Gov. Stanford, which came to California in pieces by ship, around Cape Horn

ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.q: What is a cab-forward at the California State Railroad Museum?
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.a: It's a 1944 steam locomotive with the engineer's cab at the front. The museum has the only surviving Southern Pacific cab-forward.
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.quote: the only surviving Southern Pacific cab-forward, a 1944 steam locomotive with the engineer's cab at the front

ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.q: What is the Crocker Art Museum connected to the railroad?
alts: Why is it connected to it?
Where did the art museum come from?
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.a: The railroad's lawyer, Edwin Crocker, spent his railroad fortune on art. His family's gallery became the Crocker Art Museum, the oldest art museum in the western United States.
ca519-california-state-railroad-museum.quote: spent his railroad fortune on art, and his family's gallery became the Crocker Art Museum, the oldest art museum in the western United States

alts: Which rivers is it where they come together?
What rivers are we crossing, Dad?
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.a: The American River flows into the Sacramento River near here. The freeway crosses the American River close to where the two meet.
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.quote: The freeway crosses the American River here, close to where it flows into the Sacramento.

ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.q: Why was the American River once called the River of Wounds?
alts: Why did they call that river that name?
Why would a river be named after wounds?
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.a: A Spanish expedition under Gabriel Moraga named it the Rio de las Llagas, the River of Wounds. It was perhaps because of hostile encounters with Native people.
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.quote: A Spanish expedition under Gabriel Moraga named it the Rio de las Llagas, the River of Wounds, perhaps because of hostile encounters with Native people.

ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.q: Who has lived along the American River?
alts: Were there Native people by this river?
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.a: Maidu, Miwok, Nisenan and Wintun peoples have lived along the American River for at least 5,000 years. The Nisenan call it Kum Sayo, roundhouse river.
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.quote: Maidu, Miwok, Nisenan and Wintun peoples have lived along the American River for at least 5,000 years, and the Nisenan call it Kum Sayo, roundhouse river.

ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.q: What happened where the two rivers meet in 1839?
alts: What did John Sutter do there?
Who showed up there in the old days?
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.a: John Sutter arrived at the meeting of the rivers on August 13, 1839. The next year his party built Sutter's Fort.
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.quote: On August 13, 1839, John Sutter arrived at the meeting of the rivers, and the next year his party built Sutter's Fort.

ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.q: What is special about Discovery Park at the meeting of the rivers?
alts: Why is it designed to flood?
Does that park really go underwater?
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.a: Discovery Park is designed to flood. In winter high water it can end up underwater, which takes pressure off the American River levees.
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.quote: The park at the meeting of the two rivers, Discovery Park, is designed to flood.

ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.q: Do people still use the American River today?
alts: Do we drink the water from it?
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.a: Yes. Today the American River is the main source of drinking water for Sacramento.
ca521-where-two-rivers-meet.quote: Today the American River is the main source of drinking water for Sacramento.

alts: Who used to play at it?
What team lived at that big arena, Dad?
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.a: The Sacramento Kings called ARCO Arena home from 1988 to 2016, before they moved to the new Golden 1 Center downtown.
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.quote: home of the Sacramento Kings from 1988 to 2016

ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.q: What was ARCO Arena famous for?
alts: Why do people remember that place, Mom?
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.a: In 2013 it set a Guinness World Record for the loudest sports roar, at 126 decibels.
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.quote: In 2013 it set a Guinness World Record for the loudest sports roar, at 126 decibels.

ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.q: What else happened at ARCO Arena besides basketball?
alts: Did they have fun stuff there, Mom?
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.a: It hosted concerts, ice shows, rodeos and monster truck rallies. At one point nearly two million people a year came through its doors.
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.quote: It hosted concerts, ice shows, rodeos and monster truck rallies, and at one time nearly two million people a year came through its doors.

ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.q: Did anyone famous play at ARCO Arena?
alts: Did a star player play at it?
Did any famous basketball guy play there, Dad?
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.a: LeBron James played his first regular-season NBA game there on October 29, 2003. He scored 25 points in a loss to the Kings.
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.quote: LeBron James played his first regular-season NBA game here on October 29, 2003, scoring 25 points in a loss to the Kings.

ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.q: Is ARCO Arena still there today?
alts: Can we still go see it?
Can we go inside it, Mom?
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.a: No, it was torn down in 2022. The site was donated in 2021 to California Northstate University for a medical school and hospital.
ca524-arco-arena-gone-but-loud.quote: The site was donated in 2021 to California Northstate University for a medical school and hospital

ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.q: When did Sacramento International Airport open?
alts: How old is the airport, Dad?
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.a: Sacramento International Airport opened on October 21, 1967, with a single 8,600-foot runway.
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.quote: Sacramento International Airport, just north of the freeway, opened on October 21, 1967, with a single 8,600-foot runway.

ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.q: What is the big red rabbit at the airport?
alts: Why is there a giant bunny in the airport?
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.a: It's a sculpture called Leap, a 56-foot red rabbit by the artist Lawrence Argent. It's made to look as if it jumped into Terminal B from outside.
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.quote: Leap, a 56-foot red rabbit by the artist Lawrence Argent, made to look as if it had jumped into the building from outside.

ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.q: How heavy is the red rabbit sculpture?
alts: Is the giant bunny really heavy?
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.a: Leap weighs about 10,000 pounds. It's made of aluminum, steel, granite and bronze.

ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.q: Why is there a red rabbit at the Sacramento airport?
alts: Why did they put that rabbit there?
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.a: The airport leaves that question unanswered, so visitors can make up their own story about the red rabbit.
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.quote: the airport leaves the question of why a red rabbit unanswered, so visitors can make up their own story.

ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.q: How big is Sacramento International Airport?
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.a: It covers about 6,000 acres, which is said to make it the largest commercial airport in California by land area.
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.quote: Today it covers about 6,000 acres, which is said to make it the largest commercial airport in California by land area.

ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.q: What was Sacramento International Airport first called?
alts: What was the airport's old name, Mom?
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.a: It opened as Sacramento Metropolitan Airport, with five airlines, and took over from the old municipal airport, now Sacramento Executive Airport.
ca528-airport-and-the-big-red-rabbit.quote: The airport opened as Sacramento Metropolitan Airport with five airlines

ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.q: What bridge are we crossing over the Sacramento River?
alts: What's the name of this bridge?
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.a: This is the Elkhorn Bridge, which is also called the Vietnam Servicemen Memorial Bridge. It carries the freeway across the river.
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.quote: on the Elkhorn Bridge, built in 1969 and also called the Vietnam Servicemen Memorial Bridge.

ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.q: How old is the bridge over the Sacramento River?
alts: Is this bridge really old, Buddy?
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.a: The Elkhorn Bridge was built in 1969.
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.quote: on the Elkhorn Bridge, built in 1969 and also called the Vietnam Servicemen Memorial Bridge.

ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.q: How big is the Sacramento River?
alts: Is this a really big river?
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.a: It's the largest river in California. It flows about 400 miles from the Klamath Mountains to the Delta and drains some 26,500 square miles.
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.quote: The Sacramento is the largest river in California. It flows about 400 miles from the Klamath Mountains to the Delta

ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.q: Why is it called the Sacramento River?
alts: Why does the river have that name, Buddy?
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.a: In 1808 the Spanish explorer Gabriel Moraga named it the Rio del Santisimo Sacramento, the river of the Most Holy Sacrament.
ca531-crossing-the-sacramento-river.quote: In 1808 the Spanish explorer Gabriel Moraga named it the Rio del Santisimo Sacramento, the river of the Most Holy Sacrament.

alts: What is that wide flat area?
Is that a lake or a field, what is it?
ca531-yolo-bypass.a: It's a floodway 41 miles long and about 3 miles wide. When the Sacramento River runs high, water spills into it, and it can turn into an inland sea.
ca531-yolo-bypass.quote: The Elkhorn Causeway here crosses the Yolo Bypass, a floodway 41 miles long and about 3 miles wide.

ca531-yolo-bypass.q: Why does the Yolo Bypass flood on purpose?
alts: Why do they let it fill with water, mom?
ca531-yolo-bypass.a: It takes pressure off the levees and lowers the flood risk for Sacramento and Davis. It can carry about four times the river's own flow.
ca531-yolo-bypass.quote: That takes pressure off the levees and lowers the flood risk for Sacramento and Davis.

ca531-yolo-bypass.q: How old are the weirs at the Yolo Bypass?
alts: How old is that stuff, is it really old?
ca531-yolo-bypass.a: The Sacramento Weir was built in 1916, and the two-mile-long Fremont Weir was finished in 1929.
ca531-yolo-bypass.quote: The two main weirs are the Sacramento Weir, built in 1916

ca531-yolo-bypass.q: What grows in the Yolo Bypass?
alts: What do they farm in it?
What are those crops, what's growing there?
ca531-yolo-bypass.a: In late spring and summer much of it is farmed, mostly in rice, along with safflower, tomatoes, corn and sunflowers.
ca531-yolo-bypass.quote: In late spring and summer much of the bypass is farmed, mostly in rice, along with safflower, tomatoes, corn and sunflowers.

ca531-yolo-bypass.q: What wildlife lives in the Yolo Bypass?
alts: Are there fish or birds out there?
ca531-yolo-bypass.a: Young Chinook salmon grow much faster there than in the river itself. It also holds the Vic Fazio Yolo Wildlife Area, a haven for waterfowl, shorebirds and wading birds.
ca531-yolo-bypass.quote: young Chinook salmon grow much faster in the bypass than in the river itself.

alts: Who made this town, anyone know?
ca536-knights-landing.a: Dr. William Knight, a physician from Baltimore, founded it in 1843. He built it on a mound that had long been a meeting place for the Native people living around Cache Creek and the river.
ca536-knights-landing.quote: Dr. William Knight, a physician from Baltimore, founded it in 1843 on a mound that had long been a meeting place for the Native people

ca536-knights-landing.q: Why did Knights Landing lose the name Baltimore?
alts: Why isn't it called that anymore?
Why did they change the name, was somebody mad?
What happened to the old name?
ca536-knights-landing.a: When the town was laid out in 1849 it was named Baltimore, but a dispute over selling the town lots cost it that name.
ca536-knights-landing.quote: When the town was laid out in 1849 it was named Baltimore, but a dispute over selling the town lots cost it that name.

ca536-knights-landing.q: Who lived around Knights Landing before the town?
alts: Were there Indians here before, who?
ca536-knights-landing.a: This is Patwin homeland. A Patwin group called the Yolotoi lived near Woodland and close to present-day Knights Landing, and the town's mound was a long-time meeting place.
ca536-knights-landing.quote: This is Patwin homeland, and a Patwin group called the Yolotoi lived near Woodland and close to present-day Knights Landing.

ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.q: How old is the Woodland tomato cannery?
alts: How long has it been around?
How old is that place, like really old?
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.a: Tomatoes have been processed and canned there since 1958, so it has been running for a long time.
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.quote: Tomatoes have been processed and canned here since 1958, under owners including Contadina and Del Monte

ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.q: Who owns the Woodland tomato cannery?
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.a: Pacific Coast Producers has run it since 2001. Earlier owners included Contadina and Del Monte.
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.quote: under owners including Contadina and Del Monte, and Pacific Coast Producers has run it since 2001

ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.q: How many tomatoes does the Woodland tomato cannery handle?
alts: How much does it process in a year?
How many tomatoes is that, a million?
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.a: About 495,000 tons of tomatoes a year, which is close to a billion pounds in about three months.
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.quote: handles about 495,000 tons of tomatoes a year. That is close to a billion pounds of tomatoes in about three months.

ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.q: When does the Woodland tomato cannery operate?
alts: Is it only busy part of the year?
When do they make the tomatoes?
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.a: It works in season, generally July through September.
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.quote: It works in season, generally July through September

ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.q: How does the Woodland tomato cannery deal with all its water?
alts: What do they do with the dirty water from it?
Where does the tomato wash water go?
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.a: Recycled water from the cooling towers makes up about 30 percent of the daily wash water. Wastewater is sprinkled over about 900 acres of fields, mostly grasses like Bermuda grass.
ca537-woodland-tomato-cannery.quote: recycled water from the plant's cooling towers makes up about 30 percent of each day's wash water.

ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.q: Why is Woodland called the City of Trees?
alts: Why does it call itself that?
Why do they say it's full of trees, Dad?
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.a: Woodland calls itself the City of Trees because of the valley oaks that were planted around town.
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.quote: Woodland is the county seat of Yolo County and calls itself the City of Trees, for the valley oaks planted around town.

ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.q: How did Woodland get its name?
alts: Who picked the name Woodland, Mom?
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.a: Frank Freeman bought the Yolo City store in 1857 and gave land to anyone who would clear it and build a home. In 1859 he suggested the name Woodland.
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.quote: Frank Freeman bought it in 1857, gave land to anyone who would clear it and build a home, and in 1859 suggested the name Woodland.

ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.q: How did Woodland first get started?
alts: Who built the first thing there, Mom?
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.a: In 1853 Henry Wyckoff built a store here called Yolo City. Frank Freeman bought it in 1857, and the town later became Woodland.
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.quote: In 1853 Henry Wyckoff built a store here called Yolo City. Frank Freeman bought it in 1857

ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.q: Why did Woodland become the county seat?
alts: How did it get to be the county seat?
Was there some kind of flood, Dad?
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.a: Woodland took over as county seat of Yolo County in 1862, after a flood hit the old seat at Washington, which is now part of West Sacramento.
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.quote: Woodland took over as county seat in 1862, after a flood hit the old seat at Washington, now part of West Sacramento.

ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.q: What was Woodland's economy built on?
alts: What did people do for work there?
Did they have rice or tomatoes, Mom?
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.a: For decades Woodland grew on farming, with three rice mills, a sugar beet refinery and a tomato cannery. In the 1950s it was said to have the most millionaires per capita in California.
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.quote: For decades it grew on farming, with three rice mills, a sugar beet refinery and a tomato cannery

ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.q: What is special about the Woodland Opera House?
alts: Is it worth seeing the opera house?
Did anyone famous play there, Dad?
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.a: It was the first opera house to serve the Sacramento Valley, and John Philip Sousa and his band played there. It closed in 1913, but as a state historic park it puts on shows again.
ca537-woodland-city-of-trees.quote: was the first opera house to serve the Sacramento Valley, and John Philip Sousa and his band played there.

ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.q: Who are the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation?
alts: Who are they, the people who live there?
Who lives in the Capay Valley, anyway?
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.a: They are a federally recognized Patwin tribe, and the valley is the traditional home of Patwin, or southern Wintun, people. The tribe is headquartered in Brooks, in the valley.
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.quote: it is home to the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation, a federally recognized Patwin tribe. The tribe is headquartered in Brooks, in the valley

ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.q: What was traditional Patwin life like in the Capay Valley?
alts: What did they do there long ago?
What did the Native kids eat back then?
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.a: Traditional Patwin life included fishing for king salmon, harvesting acorns, hunting and gathering.
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.quote: Traditional Patwin life included fishing for king salmon, harvesting acorns, hunting and gathering.

ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.q: What does the Yocha Dehe tribe do in the Capay Valley today?
alts: What do they do there now?
Do they still grow stuff there?
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.a: The tribe runs the Cache Creek Casino Resort in Brooks. It also farms, growing wine grapes and olives and selling olive oil, vinegar and wine under its Seka Hills brand.
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.quote: Today the tribe also farms, growing wine grapes and olives and selling olive oil, vinegar and wine under its Seka Hills brand.

ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.q: What creek runs through the Capay Valley?
alts: Is there a river in it?
Is there water there, like a creek?
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.a: Cache Creek flows through the Capay Valley. You reach the valley by taking Highway 16 west past Esparto.
ca541-capay-valley-yocha-dehe-homeland.quote: Highway 16 heads west past Esparto into the Capay Valley, which Cache Creek flows through.

ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.q: Why is it called Cache Creek?
alts: Why's it called Cache, like hiding stuff?
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.a: Hudson's Bay Company fur trappers cached, or hid, their furs along the Sacramento River and its smaller streams. They called this one Riviere la Cache.
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.quote: Its name comes from Hudson's Bay Company fur trappers, who cached, or hid, their furs along the Sacramento River and its smaller streams.

alts: Who called this creek Cache, kid-style: who named it?
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.a: Hudson's Bay Company fur trappers. They called it Riviere la Cache, after the furs they cached, or hid, along the rivers and streams.
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.quote: They called this one Riviere la Cache.

alts: Is that creek really long, how long?
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.a: Cache Creek runs 87 miles, from the outlet of Clear Lake through a canyon and the Capay Valley, then out across the valley floor.
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.quote: Cache Creek runs 87 miles from the outlet of Clear Lake, through a canyon and the Capay Valley, then out across the valley floor.

ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.q: Did people use Cache Creek before the trappers?
alts: Was it used before the trappers came?
Did Native people use that creek, like way back?
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.a: Yes. It was a trade route long before the trappers came. The main trading trail of the Patwin followed the creek.
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.quote: The creek was a trade route long before the trappers came: the main trading trail of the Patwin followed it.

ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.q: Is Cache Creek still used today?
alts: Is it still used for anything?
Do farms use that water, or is it just a creek?
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.a: Yes. A diversion dam built near Capay in 1914 sends its water through about 175 miles of canals across Yolo County.
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.quote: A diversion dam built near Capay in 1914 sends its water through about 175 miles of canals across Yolo County.

ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.q: Did the 1906 earthquake affect Cache Creek?
alts: What happened to it in the earthquake?
Did the creek get blocked, like by a landslide?
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.a: Yes. The 1906 San Francisco earthquake set off a landslide that briefly dammed the creek upstream, north of Rumsey.
ca541-cache-creek-the-trappers-creek.quote: In 1906 the San Francisco earthquake set off a landslide that briefly dammed the creek upstream, north of Rumsey.

ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.q: Where does the name Yolo come from?
alts: Where did it get that name?
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.a: It comes from the Patwin language, though nobody is quite sure of the exact source. One idea is Yo-loy, said to mean a place abounding in rushes.
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.quote: the name comes from the Patwin language. Nobody is quite sure of its source. It may come from Yo-loy, said to mean a place abounding in rushes

alts: Did it have a different name before?
Did Yolo have other names, like nicknames?
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.a: No. Before it settled on Yolo, the town went by Cacheville, Cochran's Crossing, Hutton's Ranch and Travelers Home.
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.quote: Before it settled on Yolo, the town went by Cacheville, Cochran's Crossing, Hutton's Ranch and Travelers Home.

ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.q: How many people live in Yolo?
alts: How big is it, how many people live there?
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.a: It's a little town. About 425 people lived there at the 2020 census.
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.quote: About 425 people lived here at the 2020 census.

alts: How old is it, the county there?
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.a: Yolo County was one of California's original counties, created at statehood in 1850.
ca542-yolo-place-of-rushes.quote: Yolo County was one of California's original counties, created at statehood in 1850.

alts: What exit do we take for it?

ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.q: What are the sunflower seed fields for?
alts: What are they growing those sunflowers for?
Are those sunflowers for eating, Dad?
ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.a: These sunflowers aren't grown for snacks. Some fields in this part of the valley grow sunflowers for planting seed.
ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.quote: Some fields in this part of the valley grow sunflowers for planting seed, not for snacks.

ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.q: How much of the sunflower seed comes from California?
alts: Is that a lot of the country's sunflower seed?
Does the whole world get seeds from here?
How big is California's sunflower seed business?
ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.a: California has historically produced about 95 percent of the hybrid sunflower seed planted in the United States, and a quarter of the world's supply.
ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.quote: California has historically produced about 95 percent of the hybrid sunflower seed planted in the United States, and a quarter of the world's supply

ca548-sunflower-seed-fields.q: How do bees help the sunflower seed fields?
alts: Do the bees do something with it?
