ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.a: The country around Castle Crags is the ancestral home of the Okwanuchu Shasta people. The Wintu, Achumawi and Modoc peoples have long revered the Crags too.
ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.quote: The country around Castle Crags is the ancestral home of the Okwanuchu Shasta people. The Crags have long been revered by the Wintu, Achumawi and Modoc peoples too

ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.q: What happened in the 1855 battle at Battle Rock?
alts: Was there a real fight here, Dad?
ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.a: In June 1855, miners fought Modoc people below Battle Rock. The spot is now marked at the state park entrance.
ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.quote: in June 1855 miners fought Modoc people below Battle Rock, now marked at the state park entrance.

ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.q: Is Battle Rock a historic landmark?
alts: Is that rock a big deal?
Does it have a landmark number?
ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.a: Yes, Battle Rock is California Historical Landmark No. 116.
ca723-homeland-and-the-1855-battle.quote: Battle Rock is California Historical Landmark No. 116.

ca724-castle-crags-state-park.q: How did Castle Crags State Park get started?
alts: Why is there a park here, mom?
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.a: In 1943 the state bought 925 acres of the old springs property, which was the start of Castle Crags State Park. Before that, the spring water had been bottled and shipped all over the world.
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.quote: in 1943 the state bought 925 acres of the old springs property. That was the start of Castle Crags State Park

ca724-castle-crags-state-park.q: What was the mineral water at Castle Crags used for?
alts: What was that water used for?
Why did people want the spring water?
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.a: In the 1890s, mineral water from a spring here was bottled and shipped all over the world. Native people used the spring long before anyone bottled it.
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.quote: In the 1890s, mineral water from a spring here was bottled and shipped all over the world.

ca724-castle-crags-state-park.q: What happened to the bottling company at Castle Crags?
alts: Why did the water company stop, dad?
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.a: The bottling company went broke in the 1929 crash. The bottling works had been founded back in 1889.
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.quote: The bottling company went broke in the 1929 crash

ca724-castle-crags-state-park.q: What can we do at Castle Crags State Park?
alts: Is there stuff to do for kids?
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.a: The park has 28 miles of trails and a vista point facing the Crags and Mount Shasta. The Crags Trail climbs to the base of Castle Dome.
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.quote: which has 28 miles of trails and a vista point facing the Crags and Mount Shasta

ca724-castle-crags-state-park.q: Does the mineral spring at Castle Crags still bubble up?
alts: Is the water still there, and does it stink?
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.a: Yes, the water still bubbles up with a sulfur smell. In the 1930s the Civilian Conservation Corps built a stone enclosure around it.
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.quote: the Civilian Conservation Corps built a stone enclosure around it, and the water still bubbles up with a sulfur smell

ca724-castle-crags-state-park.q: Is the Pacific Crest Trail at Castle Crags State Park?
alts: Does that trail go through it?
Can we walk a famous trail there?
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.a: Yes, today the Pacific Crest Trail winds through the park.
ca724-castle-crags-state-park.quote: Today the Pacific Crest Trail winds through the park

ca726-castle-crags.q: How old are the Castle Crags?
alts: How long ago did those spires form, like in dinosaur times?
ca726-castle-crags.a: California State Parks puts the spires' age at more than 170 million years. The granite formed underground in the Jurassic period, the age of dinosaurs.
ca726-castle-crags.quote: California State Parks puts the spires' age at more than 170 million years.

ca726-castle-crags.q: How did the Castle Crags get their shape?
alts: How did it get shaped like that?
What made those pointy rocks, Ice Age stuff?
ca726-castle-crags.a: The granite formed underground, and Ice Age glaciers later scraped away the softer rock around it, leaving the spires standing.
ca726-castle-crags.quote: Ice Age glaciers later scraped away the softer rock around it.

ca726-castle-crags.q: How tall are the Castle Crags?
alts: How high do those big rocks go?
ca726-castle-crags.a: The spires rise from about 2,000 feet at the river to more than 6,500 feet at the top.
ca726-castle-crags.quote: These granite spires rise from about 2,000 feet at the river to more than 6,500 feet at the top.

ca726-castle-crags.q: What is the round hump among the Castle Crags?
alts: What's that round part of it?
What's that big bald dome thing in the rocks?
ca726-castle-crags.a: That's Castle Dome, shaped as huge curved slabs of granite peeled away.
ca726-castle-crags.quote: The rounded hump among the spires is Castle Dome, shaped as huge curved slabs of granite peeled away.

ca726-castle-crags.q: What plants grow at Castle Crags that grow nowhere else?
alts: Does anything grow only at it?
Are there any special flowers there?
ca726-castle-crags.a: A bellflower grows here and is found nowhere else in the world. A second plant, the Castle Crags ivesia, also grows only here.
ca726-castle-crags.quote: A bellflower that grows here is found nowhere else in the world.

ca726-castle-crags.q: What is the Castle Crags Wilderness?
alts: Is that a park or something?
ca726-castle-crags.a: Much of the Crags lies in the Castle Crags Wilderness, set aside by Congress in 1984. Its northern part has bowls carved by glaciers.
ca726-castle-crags.quote: Much of the Crags lies in the Castle Crags Wilderness, set aside by Congress in 1984.

ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.q: Can you really sleep in a caboose at this stop?
alts: Mom, can we sleep in a real train?
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.a: Yes. A lodge just off this exit lets guests sleep in old cabooses, and it also has vintage cabins and campsites if you want something different.
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.quote: a lodge founded in 1968 lets guests sleep in old cabooses and eat in a restaurant inside an original train car

ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.q: How old is the Sleep in a caboose lodge?
alts: Is this place really old, Dad?
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.quote: a lodge founded in 1968 lets guests sleep in old cabooses and eat in a restaurant inside an original train car

ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.q: What was the Sleep in a caboose lodge called before?
alts: Why did the name change, Mom?
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.a: It was once called Railroad Park Resort, and it now goes by Jubilee Railroad.
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.quote: Once called Railroad Park Resort, it now goes by Jubilee Railroad.

ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.q: Where do you eat at the Sleep in a caboose lodge?
alts: Do we eat in a train too?
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.a: The restaurant is inside an original train car. Its dining car also has outdoor seats where diners can gaze up at the Crags.
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.quote: Its dining car has outdoor seats where diners can gaze up at the Crags.

ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.q: How big is the Sleep in a caboose property?
alts: Is it a huge place, Dad?
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.a: The property covers 43 acres in a forested, spring-fed creek valley.
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.quote: The property covers 43 acres in a forested, spring-fed creek valley.

ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.q: What is special about the nature around the Sleep in a caboose lodge?
alts: Are there cool animals and plants there?
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.a: The lodge calls itself the eastern gateway to the Klamath Knot, a global hot spot for plant and animal variety.
ca728-sleep-in-a-caboose.quote: The lodge calls itself the eastern gateway to the Klamath Knot, a global hot spot for plant and animal variety.

ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.q: Why is Dunsmuir called the railroad town?
alts: Why is it called a railroad town?
Why do they say trains here, what's the deal?
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.a: Dunsmuir was a railroad town first. Extra steam engines were added here to push trains up the steep grades north of town, which earned it the nickname Pusher.
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.quote: Dunsmuir was a railroad town first, nicknamed Pusher, because extra steam engines were added here to push trains up the steep grades north of town.

ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.q: How did Dunsmuir get its name?
alts: How did it get that name?
Who is Dunsmuir, was he a real person?
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.a: It's named for Alexander Dunsmuir, son of a British Columbia coal baron. In 1888 he offered the town a fountain if it would take his name.
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.quote: In 1888, Alexander Dunsmuir, son of a British Columbia coal baron, offered the town a fountain if it would take his name.

ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.q: What can we see in Dunsmuir?
alts: What is there to see in it?
Is there anything cool to look at, like trains?
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.a: The depot houses a railroad museum, the town still has an operating turntable, and three drinking fountains line Dunsmuir Avenue. Downtown is a historic district too.
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.quote: The depot houses a railroad museum, and the town still has an operating turntable. Three drinking fountains line Dunsmuir Avenue.

ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.q: Why does downtown Dunsmuir look so old?
alts: Why does it look so old-fashioned?
Why does the town look like an old movie?
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.a: When the railroad switched from steam to diesel in the 1950s, it needed fewer workers and the town shrank. That left downtown looking much as it did in the 1920s and 1930s.
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.quote: When the railroad switched from steam to diesel in the 1950s, it no longer needed so many workers here, and the town shrank.

ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.q: How big was Dunsmuir in the old days?
alts: How big was it back then?
Was this ever a big city, or always tiny?
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.a: In the early 1900s it was the largest town in Siskiyou County. For a long time it was the largest California city north of Sacramento.
ca729-dunsmuir-the-railroad-town.quote: In the early 1900s, Dunsmuir was the largest town in Siskiyou County, and for a long time the largest California city north of Sacramento.

alts: Is that a park or what?
ca730-upper-soda-springs.a: It's a riverside park in north Dunsmuir, under the freeway. Long ago it was a river crossing, then home to a toll bridge, a stage hotel and a springhouse serving soda water.
ca730-upper-soda-springs.quote: Under the freeway in north Dunsmuir lies Upper Soda Springs, now a riverside park.

ca730-upper-soda-springs.q: Who built the toll bridge at Upper Soda Springs?
alts: Was there a bridge here once?
ca730-upper-soda-springs.a: Ross and Mary Campbell McCloud built a toll bridge across the Sacramento River around 1855.
ca730-upper-soda-springs.quote: Ross and Mary Campbell McCloud built the toll bridge across the Sacramento around 1855.

ca730-upper-soda-springs.q: What's the Dolly Varden trout story at Upper Soda Springs?
alts: What's the Dolly Varden thing about it?
Who named the Dolly Varden fish?
ca730-upper-soda-springs.a: Elda McCloud, daughter of Ross and Mary McCloud, was the first to call a colorful local fish the Dolly Varden trout.
ca730-upper-soda-springs.quote: Their daughter, Elda McCloud, was the first to call a colorful local fish the Dolly Varden trout.

ca730-upper-soda-springs.q: Why did the Upper Soda Springs resort close?
alts: What happened to the old resort?
ca730-upper-soda-springs.a: Well-to-do Victorian travelers once came to take the waters, but the resort closed by 1920 as cars changed vacation habits.
ca730-upper-soda-springs.quote: Well-to-do Victorian travelers came to take the waters, but the resort closed by 1920 as cars changed vacation habits.

ca730-upper-soda-springs.q: What kind of history happened at Upper Soda Springs?
ca730-upper-soda-springs.a: Ewing Young's cattle drive stopped here in the 1830s, and the U.S. Exploring Expedition passed through in 1841. In the 1850s, Wintu people fleeing miners settled near the springs.
ca730-upper-soda-springs.quote: Ewing Young's cattle drive stopped here in the 1830s, and the U.S. Exploring Expedition passed through in 1841.

ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.q: What did Babe Ruth do in Dunsmuir?
alts: Did Babe Ruth really play baseball here?
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.a: He played an exhibition game against the locals in the city park.
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.quote: played an exhibition game against the locals in the city park

ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.q: Who came to Dunsmuir with Babe Ruth?
alts: Who was the other player with him?
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.a: Fellow New York Yankees star Bob Meusel came along on the same barnstorming tour.
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.quote: New York Yankees stars Babe Ruth and Bob Meusel came to Dunsmuir on a barnstorming tour

ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.q: What is the Babe Ruth park in Dunsmuir like today?
alts: What's in the park these days?
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.a: The park is now home to a botanical garden along the river. It covers about 10 acres and is looked after by a nonprofit group of volunteers.
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.quote: Dunsmuir City Park and Botanical Gardens covers about 10 acres. A nonprofit group of volunteers looks after the gardens.

ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.q: Is there a big league player from Dunsmuir?
alts: Did anyone from there play pro ball?
Who else is famous from Dunsmuir?
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.a: Yes, outfielder Ray Coleman was born in Dunsmuir and made it to the big leagues.
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.quote: Dunsmuir also has a big leaguer of its own: outfielder Ray Coleman was born here.

ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.q: What exit is Dunsmuir, where Babe Ruth played?
alts: What exit do we take for it?
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.a: Babe Ruth in Dunsmuir is at exit 731.
ca731-babe-ruth-in-dunsmuir.quote: Name: Babe Ruth in Dunsmuir Kind: oddity Exit: 731

ca732-hedge-creek-falls.q: Can you really walk behind Hedge Creek Falls?
alts: Mom, can we go behind the waterfall?
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.a: Yes. A short trail from the exit leads to the waterfall, and there's a small cave behind it, so you can walk behind the falling water.
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.quote: A short trail from this exit leads to a waterfall with a small cave behind it, so you can walk behind the falling water.

ca732-hedge-creek-falls.q: Why is Hedge Creek Falls called the Million Dollar Waterfall?
alts: Why is it a million dollars, Dad?
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.a: I-5's original plans would have buried the falls. Locals objected so strongly that the freeway was moved farther into the hill, at a cost of about a million dollars.
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.quote: Locals objected so strongly that the freeway was moved farther into the hill, at a cost of about a million dollars

ca732-hedge-creek-falls.q: How did the cave behind Hedge Creek Falls form?
alts: How did that cave get there?
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.a: The falls pour over the tip of an old lava flow from Mount Shasta. The cave is a natural hollow in that thick lava, not something carved by splashing water.
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.quote: the cave is a natural hollow in that thick lava, not something carved by splashing water

ca732-hedge-creek-falls.q: What happened at Hedge Creek Falls with Black Bart?
alts: What did that robber do here?
Was there a bad guy at the waterfall?
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.a: In October 1879, stagecoach robber Black Bart held up a stage near Dunsmuir, and evidence suggested he hid in this cave first. He wore a flour sack mask and was known for being polite.
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.quote: In October 1879, the stagecoach robber Black Bart held up the Roseburg to Redding stage near Dunsmuir, and evidence suggested he hid in this cave first.

ca732-hedge-creek-falls.q: What else is there to see at Hedge Creek Falls besides the waterfall?
alts: What else is there at it?
Is there anything else to see there?
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.a: There's a viewing platform over the river with a view of Mount Shasta.
ca732-hedge-creek-falls.quote: There's also a viewing platform over the river with a view of Mount Shasta.

alts: What was this place, like a hotel?
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.a: It was a summer resort on the railroad main line in the late 1800s and early 1900s, just north of Dunsmuir.
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.quote: Just north of Dunsmuir was Shasta Springs, a summer resort on the railroad main line in the late 1800s and early 1900s.

ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.q: Is this really where Shasta soda began?
alts: Is that really where the soda came from?
Did the soda really start here?
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.a: Yes. Natural springs here were the original source of the water and drinks that became the Shasta brand of soft drinks.
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.quote: Natural springs here were the original source of the water and drinks that became the Shasta brand of soft drinks.

ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.q: What was at the Shasta Springs resort?
alts: What cool stuff was at the resort?
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.a: It had its own train station, an incline railway up the hillside, fountains, a kiosk and a bottling plant.
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.quote: The resort had its own train station, an incline railway up the hillside, fountains, a kiosk and a bottling plant.

ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.q: Can we visit Shasta Springs today?
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.a: No. The property now belongs to the Saint Germain Foundation and is closed to the public.
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.quote: the property now belongs to the Saint Germain Foundation and is closed to the public.

ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.q: What happened to the Shasta Springs resort?
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.a: It closed in the early 1950s. The lower resort is gone, and blackberry bushes have overgrown its ruins.

ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.q: Is it safe to hike to Mossbrae Falls from here?
alts: Can we walk to the falls from there?
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.a: Not really. The usual route means trespassing along the railroad tracks, and hikers were injured by trains there in 2011 and 2019.
ca733-where-shasta-soda-began.quote: The usual route to nearby Mossbrae Falls means trespassing along the railroad tracks, and hikers were injured by trains there in 2011 and 2019.

ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.q: What happened at the Cantara Loop?
alts: Mom, what went wrong at that loop?
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.a: A train derailed at a horseshoe curve called the Cantara Loop on the night of July 14, 1991. A tank car spilled about 19,000 gallons of pesticide into the river.
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.quote: On the night of July 14, 1991, a train derailed at a horseshoe curve called the Cantara Loop, upstream from Dunsmuir, and a tank car spilled about 19,000 gallons of pesticide into the river.

ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.q: How bad was the Cantara Loop spill?
alts: Did a lot of animals die?
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.a: It's still the largest hazardous chemical spill in California history. More than a million fish died.
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.quote: More than a million fish died. It's still the largest hazardous chemical spill in California history, but the river has largely recovered.

ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.q: What chemical spilled at the Cantara Loop?
alts: What was in the tank car?
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.a: It was a soil fumigant called metam sodium. It left a 41-mile trail of destruction all the way to Shasta Lake.
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.quote: The chemical, a soil fumigant called metam sodium, left a 41-mile trail of destruction all the way to Shasta Lake.

ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.q: What else died in the Cantara Loop spill besides fish?
alts: Did frogs and trees die too?
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.a: Tens of thousands of frogs and crayfish died, plus millions of insects and other small river creatures. Hundreds of thousands of willows, alders and cottonwoods eventually died too.
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.quote: Tens of thousands of frogs and crayfish died, along with millions of insects and other small river creatures, and hundreds of thousands of willows, alders and cottonwoods eventually died too.

ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.q: Has the river recovered from the Cantara Loop spill?
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.a: Largely, yes. The river is again open to catch-and-release fishing all year, though crayfish and frogs still have not fully returned.
ca734-the-cantara-loop-spill.quote: Crayfish and frogs still have not fully returned, but the river is again open to catch-and-release fishing all year.

ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.q: What is McCloud, the company town?
alts: Why is it called a company town?
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.a: McCloud is a lumber company town on the southern slope of Mount Shasta. For decades the company mill supplied the homes with electricity and even steam heat.
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.quote: McCloud, a lumber company town on the southern slope of Mount Shasta. For decades the company mill supplied the homes with electricity and even steam heat.

ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.q: Is the McCloud mill still running?
alts: Does the mill still make lumber?
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.a: No, the mill closed for good in 2002.
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.quote: The houses passed to private owners in 1965, and the mill closed for good in 2002.

ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.q: Why was the first McCloud mill a failure?
alts: Why couldn't they get the logs out?
What went wrong with the first mill?
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.a: The first mill, built in 1892, failed because hauling lumber over the hills by oxen was too hard. The McCloud River Railroad, founded in 1895, solved that problem.
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.quote: The first mill here, built in 1892, failed because hauling lumber over the hills by oxen was too hard. The McCloud River Railroad, founded in 1895, solved that problem.

ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.q: Is there anything historic to see in McCloud?
alts: Is there anything cool to see there?
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.a: Yes, part of downtown McCloud is on the National Register of Historic Places. There's also a statue called Joaquin's Book in Hoo Hoo Park.
ca736-mccloud-a-company-town.quote: Part of downtown McCloud is on the National Register of Historic Places. A statue called Joaquin's Book stands in McCloud's Hoo Hoo Park

ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.q: How old is the Mount Shasta trout hatchery?
alts: How long have they been raising fish here, mom?
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.a: The Mount Shasta Hatchery has raised trout since 1888. The state calls it the oldest trout hatchery west of the Mississippi.
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.quote: the Mount Shasta Hatchery has raised trout since 1888, and the state calls it the oldest trout hatchery west of the Mississippi

ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.q: What can we see at the Mount Shasta trout hatchery?
alts: What can you see at it?
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.a: From mid-March through July, visitors can watch the eggs hatch and the baby fish grow. Trout here can also grow to nearly 10 pounds.
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.quote: From mid-March through July, visitors can watch the eggs hatch and the baby fish grow.

ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.q: What was the Mount Shasta hatchery site before it raised fish?
alts: Was something else here a long time ago?
What happened here with the horses?
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.a: The same address was once the Strawberry Valley Stage Station. Stagecoach drivers got fresh horses there from 1857 until the railroad arrived in 1886.
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.quote: The same address was once the Strawberry Valley Stage Station, where stagecoach drivers got fresh horses from 1857 until the railroad arrived in 1886.

ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.q: Who was Justin Sisson at the Mount Shasta hatchery?
alts: Who was he, the postmaster guy?
Who started the first hatchery here?
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.a: Justin Sisson was the first postmaster of the Berryvale post office across the road. He built a hotel nearby in 1865 and started his own trout hatchery in 1887.
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.quote: whose first postmaster was Justin Sisson. He built a hotel nearby in 1865 and started his own trout hatchery in 1887.

ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.q: Where can we learn more about the Mount Shasta hatchery's story?
alts: Is there a museum about it?
Is there somewhere to learn the history?
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.a: The Sisson Museum tells the story of the hatchery and the area. The old stage station site is also California Historical Landmark No. 396.
ca737-mount-shasta-trout-hatchery.quote: The stage station site is California Historical Landmark No. 396.

alts: Who was that Sisson guy, dad?
ca738-mount-shasta-city.a: Justin Sisson ran the Strawberry Valley stage inn. He also gave the land for the railroad station, and the town was named Sisson after him.
ca738-mount-shasta-city.quote: Justin Sisson ran the Strawberry Valley stage inn, and the railroad's completion in 1887 brought tourists, loggers and new residents.

ca738-mount-shasta-city.q: How much snow does Mount Shasta City get?
alts: Does it get a lot of snow there?
Does it snow a ton there, mom?
ca738-mount-shasta-city.a: A typical winter brings nearly 103 inches of snow. The snowiest year on record was 1952, with 349.6 inches.
ca738-mount-shasta-city.quote: gets nearly 103 inches of snow in a typical winter.

ca738-mount-shasta-city.q: How high up is Mount Shasta City?
alts: Are we way up in the mountains there, dad?
ca738-mount-shasta-city.a: The town sits at about 3,600 feet, less than 9 miles from the summit of the mountain.
ca738-mount-shasta-city.quote: It sits at about 3,600 feet, less than 9 miles from the summit

ca738-mount-shasta-city.q: Who famous was born in Mount Shasta City?
alts: Did any famous person come from here, mom?
ca738-mount-shasta-city.a: Anita Loos, the writer behind Gentlemen Prefer Blondes, was born here in 1888, when the town was called Sisson.
ca738-mount-shasta-city.quote: Anita Loos, the writer behind Gentlemen Prefer Blondes, was born in Sisson in 1888.

ca738-mount-shasta-city.q: What's Shasta Abbey near Mount Shasta City?
alts: Is there a monastery there, dad?
ca738-mount-shasta-city.a: Shasta Abbey is a Buddhist training monastery just north of town.
ca738-mount-shasta-city.quote: Shasta Abbey, a Buddhist training monastery, sits just north of town

ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.q: Where does the water at Headwaters of the Sacramento come from?
alts: How is there water just pouring out of a hill?
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.a: It started as glacial melt and spent more than 50 years filtering through volcanic rock before pouring out of the hillside at Big Springs.
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.quote: It started as glacial melt and spent more than 50 years filtering through volcanic rock.

ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.q: How much water flows out at Headwaters of the Sacramento?
alts: How much comes out of it?
Is it a lot of water, or just a trickle?
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.a: About 12 million gallons a day flow out here, and that water helps start the Sacramento River.
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.quote: About 12 million gallons a day flow out here and help start the Sacramento River.

ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.q: Can we drink the water at Headwaters of the Sacramento?
alts: Can we taste the water, Mom?
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.a: People fill jugs there, but a sign warns the water has not been tested and may not be safe to drink.
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.quote: a sign warns that the water has not been tested and may not be safe to drink

ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.q: Can we swim or wade at Headwaters of the Sacramento?
alts: Can we splash around in the spring?
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.a: No. Wading and swimming in the spring are not allowed.
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.quote: Wading and swimming in the spring are not allowed.

ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.q: What happened here at Headwaters of the Sacramento in 1901?
alts: What did that water wheel do?
Did people long ago use the spring for something?
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.a: In 1901, a water wheel at Big Springs gave the town its first electricity, for a few street lights.
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.quote: In 1901, a water wheel at Big Springs gave the town its first electricity, for a few street lights.

ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.q: Where does the water go after Headwaters of the Sacramento?
alts: Where does the water end up, kids wonder?
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.a: It flows through the Mount Shasta Hatchery and into Lake Siskiyou before joining the Sacramento River.
ca739-headwaters-of-the-sacramento.quote: The spring water flows through the Mount Shasta Hatchery and into Lake Siskiyou before joining the Sacramento.

alts: How big is that mountain, like really big?
ca740-mount-shasta.a: Mount Shasta rises to 14,179 feet. By volume it is the biggest stratovolcano in the Cascade Range.
ca740-mount-shasta.quote: Mount Shasta rises to 14,179 feet. By volume, about 85 cubic miles, it is the biggest stratovolcano in the Cascade Range

ca740-mount-shasta.q: Is Mount Shasta an active volcano?
alts: Is that mountain going to explode?
ca740-mount-shasta.a: Its last major eruption was about 3,000 years ago, with smaller ones about 200 years ago. A 2019 report put the chance of an eruption by 2049 at 3.5 percent.
ca740-mount-shasta.quote: Smaller eruptions happened as recently as about 200 years ago, and a 2019 report put the chance of an eruption by 2049 at 3.5 percent.

alts: Is that snow on the mountain real ice?
ca740-mount-shasta.a: Yes, seven glaciers ring its slopes. The Whitney Glacier is the longest in California, and the Hotlum holds the most ice.

alts: Is the ice on it melting?
Is the snow on that mountain going away?
ca740-mount-shasta.a: A 2002 survey found that, unusually, they had grown since 1951, fed by heavier snowfall. Researchers warned that further warming would likely make them retreat.
ca740-mount-shasta.quote: A 2002 survey found that, unusually, Shasta's glaciers had grown since 1951, fed by heavier snowfall

ca740-mount-shasta.q: What is Mount Shasta's name in Native languages?
alts: What do Native people call it?
Does that mountain have another name?
ca740-mount-shasta.a: The Shasta people call it Waka-nunee-Tuki-wuki, and in the Karuk language it is Uytaahkoo.
ca740-mount-shasta.quote: The Shasta people call the mountain Waka-nunee-Tuki-wuki, and in the Karuk language it is Uytaahkoo.

ca741-the-lemurians-legend.q: What is the Lemurians legend of Mount Shasta?
alts: What's the secret city on the mountain, mom?
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.a: It's a legend that a hidden city sits on Mount Shasta, home to advanced beings from a lost continent called Lemuria. No one has ever found the city.
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.quote: a hidden city on the mountain, home to advanced beings from a lost continent called Lemuria. The story grew from a passing mention in the 1880s into a whole book in 1931.

ca741-the-lemurians-legend.q: Has anyone ever found the Lemurian city on Mount Shasta?
alts: Is the hidden city real, dad?
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.a: No. Nobody has ever found the city.
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.quote: No one has ever found the city.

ca741-the-lemurians-legend.q: Where did the idea of Lemuria come from?
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.a: It began in 1864, when a zoologist proposed a sunken continent to explain why lemur fossils turned up in both Madagascar and India.
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.quote: The idea of Lemuria began in 1864, when a zoologist proposed a sunken continent to explain why lemur fossils turned up in both Madagascar and India.

ca741-the-lemurians-legend.q: Is Lemuria a real lost continent?
alts: Did a whole continent really sink?
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.a: Scientists dropped the idea once plate tectonics explained the puzzle of the lemur fossils in Madagascar and India.
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.quote: Scientists dropped the idea once plate tectonics explained the puzzle.

ca741-the-lemurians-legend.q: How did the Lemurians legend get tied to Mount Shasta?
alts: How did it end up on Shasta?
Who put the legend on the mountain?
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.a: By 1925 writers described a hidden Lemurian village on Shasta, and a 1931 book by Harvey Spencer Lewis, written under a pen name, cemented the legend.
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.quote: By 1925 writers described a hidden Lemurian village on Shasta, and a 1931 book by Harvey Spencer Lewis, written under a pen name, cemented the legend.

ca741-the-lemurians-legend.q: Are there older legends about Mount Shasta?
alts: Is there an older story about it?
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.a: Yes. The Klamath Tribes tell much older stories of Skell, the Spirit of the Above-World, living on the mountain and battling Llao of Mount Mazama with hot rocks and lava.
ca741-the-lemurians-legend.quote: Much older are the stories of the Klamath Tribes, which tell of Skell, the Spirit of the Above-World, living on the mountain and battling Llao of Mount Mazama with hot rocks and lava.

alts: How long ago did that thing form, like, a million years?
ca742-black-butte.a: Black Butte is a cluster of lava domes that squeezed out about 9,000 to 10,000 years ago.
ca742-black-butte.quote: a cluster of lava domes that squeezed out about 9,000 to 10,000 years ago

ca742-black-butte.q: What other names has Black Butte had?
alts: Did it ever have a different name?
Does that mountain have any other names, like funny ones?
ca742-black-butte.a: Over the years it has also been called Wintoon Butte, Cone Mountain, Sugar Loaf and Muir's Peak.
ca742-black-butte.quote: Over the years it has also been called Wintoon Butte, Cone Mountain, Sugar Loaf and Muir's Peak.

ca742-black-butte.q: Was there ever a fire lookout on Black Butte?
alts: Did they have a lookout on it?
Was there a little house on top of that mountain?
ca742-black-butte.a: Yes. A Forest Service fire lookout stood on top from the early 1930s until the Columbus Day Storm of 1962 destroyed it. A new one was used from 1963 to 1973.
ca742-black-butte.quote: A Forest Service fire lookout stood on top from the early 1930s until the Columbus Day Storm of 1962 destroyed it.

ca742-black-butte.q: Can you hike up Black Butte?
alts: Can we walk up to the top of that mountain?
ca742-black-butte.a: Yes, a 2.5-mile trail climbs to the summit. On clear days you can see Mount McLoughlin in Oregon, 70 miles away.
ca742-black-butte.quote: A 2.5-mile trail climbs to the summit, where on clear days Mount McLoughlin in Oregon shows up 70 miles away.

ca742-black-butte.q: What is Black Butte Summit on I-5?
alts: How high is the pass at it?
How high up are we at that mountain?
ca742-black-butte.a: I-5 crosses a 3,912-foot pass at the western base of Black Butte. It is called Black Butte Summit.
ca742-black-butte.quote: I-5 crosses a 3,912-foot pass at its western base, called Black Butte Summit.

ca742-black-butte.q: What railroad lines meet at Black Butte?
alts: Is there a railroad near it?
Are there trains by that mountain?
ca742-black-butte.a: The railroad's Cascade Line by way of Klamath Falls, built in the 1920s, meets the older Siskiyou Line at Black Butte.
ca742-black-butte.quote: At Black Butte, the railroad's Cascade Line by way of Klamath Falls, built in the 1920s, meets the older Siskiyou Line.

alts: How big is that little mountain, like for real?
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.a: Shastina is about 12,330 feet tall. That's even taller than Mount Adams in Washington.
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.quote: Shastina, about 12,330 feet tall. That's taller than Mount Adams in Washington.

alts: Is that mountain, like, a million years old?
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.a: Shastina was built about 9,500 years ago, after the last ice age. That's why its summit crater is still intact.
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.quote: Shastina was built about 9,500 years ago, after the last ice age, which is why its summit crater is still intact.

alts: Why does that mountain have such a funny name?
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.a: Shastina simply means little Shasta. It's the smaller peak on Mount Shasta's west side.
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.quote: The name Shastina simply means little Shasta.

alts: What made that big gash in it?
What's that giant scratch on the mountain?
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.a: Diller Canyon is the big gash down Shastina's side facing Weed. Hot volcanic flows cut it, and it drops more than 7,000 vertical feet.
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.quote: The big gash down its side facing Weed is Diller Canyon, cut by hot volcanic flows, and it drops more than 7,000 vertical feet.

ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.q: Is there a lake on top of Shastina?
alts: Are there lakes up there on it?
Can you swim in a lake on top of the mountain?
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.a: Yes, the crater holds three small lakes, including Clarence King Lake and Sisson Lake. They're the highest open-air lakes in the whole Cascade Range.
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.quote: The crater holds three small lakes, including Clarence King Lake and Sisson Lake, the highest open-air lakes in the whole Cascade Range.

ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.q: What did Shastina's eruptions do to the land?
alts: What did it do when it erupted?
Did the volcano blow up near where towns are now?
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.a: Its eruptions, along with Black Butte's, sent hot flows across about 43 square miles. That includes much of the ground where Mount Shasta City and Weed now stand.
ca743-shastina-and-diller-canyon.quote: Its eruptions, along with those of Black Butte, sent hot flows across about 43 square miles, including much of the ground where Mount Shasta City and Weed now stand.

alts: How big is that mountain, mom?
ca744-mount-eddy.a: Mount Eddy is 9,037 feet tall, and it's the highest point in the Trinity Mountains.
ca744-mount-eddy.quote: The big peak west of the freeway is Mount Eddy, 9,037 feet tall, the highest point in the Trinity Mountains.

ca744-mount-eddy.q: Why is Mount Eddy called Mount Eddy?
alts: Who is that mountain named after?
ca744-mount-eddy.a: It's named for Olive Paddock Eddy, who is often mistakenly credited as the first woman to climb Mount Shasta.
ca744-mount-eddy.quote: Mount Eddy is named for Olive Paddock Eddy, who is often mistakenly credited with being the first woman to climb Mount Shasta

ca744-mount-eddy.q: What is Mount Eddy made of?
alts: What kind of rock is it?
What's that mountain made out of?
ca744-mount-eddy.a: It's made mostly of a rock called serpentinized peridotite.
ca744-mount-eddy.quote: It's made mostly of a rock called serpentinized peridotite.

ca744-mount-eddy.q: What did the Wintu call Mount Eddy?
ca744-mount-eddy.a: The Wintu name may have been Num-mel-be-le-sas-pam, which means west blaze mountain.
ca744-mount-eddy.quote: The Wintu name for the peak may have been Num-mel-be-le-sas-pam, west blaze mountain.

alts: How many years old is that cave, like, really old?
ca747-pluto-s-cave.a: Pluto's Cave is a lava tube roughly 190,000 years old.
ca747-pluto-s-cave.quote: Pluto's Cave, a lava tube roughly 190,000 years old.

ca747-pluto-s-cave.q: Why is it called Pluto's Cave?
alts: Is Pluto the planet or the dog? Why is it named that?
ca747-pluto-s-cave.a: It was named for Pluto, the god of the underworld.
ca747-pluto-s-cave.quote: it was named for Pluto, the god of the underworld.

alts: Did some kid find that cave?
ca747-pluto-s-cave.a: A man named Nelson Cash stumbled onto it in 1863 while he was looking for stray cattle.
ca747-pluto-s-cave.quote: A man named Nelson Cash stumbled onto it in 1863 while looking for stray cattle

ca747-pluto-s-cave.q: Can we go inside Pluto's Cave?
alts: Can we walk in the cave, is it scary?
ca747-pluto-s-cave.a: Yes, visitors can hike about 1,200 feet inside the cave.
ca747-pluto-s-cave.quote: Visitors can hike about 1,200 feet inside.

ca747-pluto-s-cave.q: What lived or was found inside Pluto's Cave?
alts: What did they find in it?
Were there animals in that cave, like bats?
ca747-pluto-s-cave.a: In 1863 the survey scientists found bats all the way to the end, and skulls of bighorn sheep near the entrance, where the roof had fallen in.
ca747-pluto-s-cave.quote: They found bats all the way to the end and skulls of bighorn sheep near the entrance, where the roof had fallen in.

ca747-pluto-s-cave.q: Why did John Muir say Pluto's Cave was hard to find?
alts: Why is it hard to find?
Why can't people find that cave?
ca747-pluto-s-cave.a: John Muir warned that it was hard to find because its openings are level with the ground.
ca747-pluto-s-cave.quote: warning that it was hard to find because its openings are level with the ground.

ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.q: Why is the town called Weed?
alts: How did Weed get such a funny name, Mom?
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.a: It's named for Abner Weed, who found that the strong winds here were good for drying lumber.
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.quote: Weed is named for Abner Weed, who found that the strong winds here were good for drying lumber.

ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.q: What is the motto of Weed?
alts: What does it say on the signs?
Does Weed have a funny slogan?
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.a: The town motto is Weed like to welcome you. Over the years its road signs have had a habit of disappearing.
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.quote: The town motto is Weed like to welcome you, and over the years its road signs have had a habit of disappearing.

ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.q: What is there to see or do in Weed?
alts: Is there anything fun to do for kids?
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.a: You can visit the Weed Historic Lumber Town Museum to see sawmill machinery from the early days. The town also holds a Carnevale every June or July, with bocce ball tournaments.
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.quote: The Weed Historic Lumber Town Museum shows sawmill machinery from the early days.

ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.q: Where does Weed get its drinking water?
alts: Where does it get water from?
Is the water from a spring or something?
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.a: The town's water comes from Beaughan Spring and is piped straight to homes.
ca747-weed-a-windy-lumber-town.quote: The town's water comes from Beaughan Spring, piped straight to homes.

ca749-weed-s-wildfires.q: What was the Boles Fire in Weed?
alts: What was that fire in Weed?
What happened to Weed in the big fire?
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.a: The Boles Fire was a wind-driven fire that spread through Weed on September 15, 2014. It destroyed more than 150 buildings in a single day, most of them homes.
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.quote: On September 15, 2014, the wind-driven Boles Fire spread through Weed and destroyed more than 150 buildings, most of them homes, in a single day.

ca749-weed-s-wildfires.q: What was the Mill Fire in Weed?
alts: What was that fire that started at the mill?
Did a fire burn down houses here too?
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.a: The Mill Fire started on September 2, 2022, at the lumber mill north of town. It burned the Lincoln Heights neighborhood.
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.quote: On September 2, 2022, the Mill Fire started at the lumber mill north of town and burned the Lincoln Heights neighborhood.

ca749-weed-s-wildfires.q: What caused the Mill Fire in Weed?
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.a: Fire officials traced it to the mill's operations. The company said a machine meant to cool hot ash from its wood-burning power plant may have failed.
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.quote: Fire officials traced the Mill Fire to the mill's operations, and the company said a machine meant to cool hot ash from its wood-burning power plant may have failed.

ca749-weed-s-wildfires.q: How much damage did the Mill Fire do?
alts: Did people get hurt in that fire?
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.a: The Mill Fire destroyed 118 structures, and two people died. It raced north into Lake Shastina.
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.quote: The fire destroyed 118 structures, and two people died. It raced north into Lake Shastina.

ca749-weed-s-wildfires.q: What was the Lava Fire near Weed?
alts: What happened on Mount Shasta in the Lava Fire?
Did a fire burn the mountain?
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.a: The 2021 Lava Fire is believed to have been started by lightning. It burned more than 26,000 acres on Mount Shasta's slopes and damaged a railroad trestle.
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.quote: In 2021, the Lava Fire, believed to have been started by lightning, burned more than 26,000 acres on Mount Shasta's slopes.

ca749-weed-s-wildfires.q: Did the Lava Fire affect the train?
alts: Why did the train stop running, Dad?
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.a: Yes. The Lava Fire damaged a railroad trestle, which disrupted Amtrak's Coast Starlight for weeks.
ca749-weed-s-wildfires.quote: It also damaged a railroad trestle, disrupting Amtrak's Coast Starlight for weeks.

ca748-a-two-block-highway.q: How long is A two-block highway?
alts: How many blocks is that, really?
ca748-a-two-block-highway.a: It's only two blocks long. That makes it the second-shortest state highway in California.
ca748-a-two-block-highway.quote: It's only two blocks long, which makes it the second-shortest state highway in California.

ca748-a-two-block-highway.q: Where does A two-block highway go?
alts: Where does it start and end?
Where does that little road lead?
ca748-a-two-block-highway.a: Route 265 runs from U.S. 97 in Weed to the North Weed interchange on I-5.
ca748-a-two-block-highway.quote: Route 265 runs from U.S. 97 in Weed to the North Weed interchange on I-5.

ca748-a-two-block-highway.q: What was A two-block highway before it was Route 265?
alts: Was that road something else once?
What did it used to be?
ca748-a-two-block-highway.a: It used to be part of U.S. Route 99.
ca748-a-two-block-highway.quote: It used to be part of U.S. Route 99.

ca748-a-two-block-highway.q: Why is A two-block highway called a hidden highway?
alts: Why was that road a secret?
How did people know it was there?
ca748-a-two-block-highway.a: For many years it had no signs at all. The only clue was a bridge number spray-painted on the I-5 overpass: 265 overcrossing.
ca748-a-two-block-highway.quote: For many years the route was hidden, with no signs at all. The only clue was a bridge number spray-painted

ca748-a-two-block-highway.q: When did A two-block highway finally get road signs?
alts: When did they put up signs for it?
When did that road get signs?
ca748-a-two-block-highway.a: Signs finally went up in 2005, in preparation for a full rebuild of Weed Boulevard.
ca748-a-two-block-highway.quote: Signs finally went up in 2005, in preparation for a full rebuild of Weed Boulevard.

ca751-gray-wolves-return.q: When did gray wolves come back to California?
alts: Wait, wolves are back in California? Since when?
ca751-gray-wolves-return.a: In late December 2011, a collared wolf from Oregon called OR-7 crossed the state line. He was the first wild wolf confirmed in California since 1924.
ca751-gray-wolves-return.quote: In late December 2011, a collared wolf from Oregon known as OR-7 crossed the state line, the first wild wolf confirmed in California since 1924.

ca751-gray-wolves-return.q: Who was OR-7, the wolf that came back to California?
alts: Did that wolf have a nickname?
ca751-gray-wolves-return.a: OR-7 was a wolf from Oregon nicknamed Journey. He wandered more than 1,000 miles from the Wallowa Mountains of northeastern Oregon.
ca751-gray-wolves-return.quote: OR-7, nicknamed Journey, had wandered more than 1,000 miles from the Wallowa Mountains of northeastern Oregon

alts: Was there a whole wolf family here?
ca751-gray-wolves-return.a: It was the state's first resident wolf pack in over a century, with two adults and five pups. The pack later vanished, and no one has explained why.
ca751-gray-wolves-return.quote: a trail camera in Siskiyou County confirmed the Shasta Pack, two adults and five pups, the state's first resident wolf pack in more than a century.

ca751-gray-wolves-return.q: How many gray wolves live in California now?
alts: Are there lots of wolves out here?
ca751-gray-wolves-return.a: By December 2025 the state counted 55 wolves in nine packs.
ca751-gray-wolves-return.quote: By December 2025 the state counted 55 wolves in nine packs.

ca751-gray-wolves-return.q: Are gray wolves protected in California?
alts: Is it against the law to hurt them?
ca751-gray-wolves-return.a: Wolves are listed as endangered in California. The state has also set aside money to pay ranchers for livestock lost to them.
ca751-gray-wolves-return.quote: Wolves are listed as endangered in California, and the state has set aside money to pay ranchers for livestock lost to them.

ca751-gray-wolves-return.q: Has California ever killed wolves that attacked cattle?
ca751-gray-wolves-return.a: Yes, in 2025, after nearly 100 tries at scaring them off, officials killed four wolves from a Plumas County pack that kept preying on cattle. It was the first time the state had done so.
ca751-gray-wolves-return.quote: In 2025, after nearly 100 tries at scaring them off, state wildlife officials killed four wolves from a Plumas County pack that kept preying on cattle, the first time the state had done so.

ca755-old-highway-99.q: What was U.S. 99 before I-5 replaced it?
alts: What was it before the freeway came along?
What was the road before this big highway, mom?
ca755-old-highway-99.a: U.S. 99 was the main West Coast highway before I-5. It ran from the Mexican border to the Canadian border, and people called it the Golden State Highway and the Main Street of California.
ca755-old-highway-99.quote: U.S. 99 was created in 1926 and ran from the Mexican border to the Canadian border. It was known as the Golden State Highway and the Main Street of California.

alts: How long ago did they build this old road?
ca755-old-highway-99.a: U.S. 99 was created in 1926. That's the road this old stretch comes from, back when it was the main West Coast highway.
ca755-old-highway-99.quote: U.S. 99 was created in 1926 and ran from the Mexican border to the Canadian border.

alts: Where did the old road go, dad?
ca755-old-highway-99.a: A 1963 bill by State Senator Randolph Collier renumbered California's highways. By 1968 the 99 route was gone, replaced here by I-5.
ca755-old-highway-99.quote: Its end began with a 1963 bill by State Senator Randolph Collier that renumbered California's highways, and by 1968 the route was gone, replaced here by I-5.

ca755-old-highway-99.q: Can you still drive on Old Highway 99?
alts: Is it still a road you can use?
Can we drive on the old road, dad?
ca755-old-highway-99.a: Yes. A two-lane county road called Old Highway 99 runs between Weed and Yreka, still in the same form it had when it was U.S. 99.
ca755-old-highway-99.quote: A two-lane county road called Old Highway 99 runs between Weed and Yreka, still in the same form it had when it was U.S. 99

ca755-old-highway-99.q: Does Old Highway 99 run next to the freeway?
alts: Is the old road right beside us, mom?
Does it go the same way?
ca755-old-highway-99.a: Roughly, yes. It parallels the freeway, but at one point it swings several miles away from it.
ca755-old-highway-99.quote: It roughly parallels the freeway, but at one point swings several miles away.

ca755-old-highway-99.q: What happened to Old Highway 99 north of Yreka?
alts: Does it keep going past Yreka?
Where does the old road go after Yreka, dad?
Is old 99 still there up north?
ca755-old-highway-99.a: North of Yreka, old 99 became State Route 263. Much of it between Hornbrook and Oregon has been torn up or sits on private land.
ca755-old-highway-99.quote: North of Yreka, old 99 became State Route 263, and much of it between Hornbrook and Oregon has been torn up or sits on private land.

ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.q: What is Gazelle's antelope name all about?
alts: Why's it called Gazelle, like the animal?
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.a: A gazelle is a small African antelope. Gazelle's post office took the name in 1870, and a steamer called the Gazelle also ran on the Sacramento River in the 1850s.
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.quote: A gazelle is a small African antelope, and in the 1850s a steamer called the Gazelle also ran between San Francisco and the upper Sacramento River.

ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.q: When did Gazelle get its name?
alts: When did it get that name?
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.a: Gazelle's post office took the name Gazelle in 1870.
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.quote: Its post office took the name Gazelle in 1870.

ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.q: How many people live in Gazelle?
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.a: Gazelle is a tiny town of about 95 people.
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.quote: West of the freeway sits Gazelle, a tiny town of about 95 people.

ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.q: What kind of land is Gazelle in?
alts: What's the land like around it?
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.a: Gazelle sits in a dry farming valley in the Shasta River's watershed. Most of the river's water there comes from groundwater and irrigation runoff.
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.quote: Gazelle lies in the Shasta River's watershed, a dry farming valley. Most of the river's water there comes from groundwater and from irrigation runoff.

ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.q: Which exit do we take for Gazelle?
ca759-gazelle-s-antelope-name.quote: Name: Gazelle's antelope name Kind: town Exit: 759

ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.q: What are the hummocks of Shasta Valley?
alts: What are those bumpy hills, Mom?
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.a: They're the little lumpy hills scattered across the flat valley. They are pieces of debris left behind when an older version of Mount Shasta collapsed in a huge landslide.
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.quote: Hundreds of thousands of years ago, an older version of Mount Shasta collapsed in one of the largest landslides known on Earth.

ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.q: How did the hummocks of Shasta Valley form?
alts: How did those hills get there?
Why are there bumpy hills in the flat valley?
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.a: An older Mount Shasta collapsed in a giant landslide, and the debris spread across the valley. The hummocks are the pieces of that debris.
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.quote: The debris spread across more than 170 square miles of Shasta Valley, and these hummocks are the pieces.

ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.q: How old are the hummocks of Shasta Valley?
alts: Did dinosaurs see those bumpy hills?
How long ago did that happen?
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.a: The landslide that made them happened hundreds of thousands of years ago, when an older version of Mount Shasta collapsed.
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.quote: Hundreds of thousands of years ago, an older version of Mount Shasta collapsed in one of the largest landslides known on Earth.

ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.q: How big was the landslide that made the Shasta Valley hummocks?
alts: Was the mountain landslide really huge, Dad?
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.a: It was one of the largest landslides known on Earth. About 6.5 cubic miles of rock flowed into the valley, spreading over more than 170 square miles.
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.quote: The collapse sent about 6.5 cubic miles of rock flowing into Shasta Valley.

ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.q: How far do the Shasta Valley hummocks stretch?
alts: How far do those hills go?
Where do the bumpy hills start and stop?
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.a: The hills reach from the base of Mount Shasta to just past Montague. The whole flow is 28 miles long.
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.quote: The hills reach from the base of the mountain to just past Montague. The Shasta River now cuts through the 28-mile-long flow.

ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.q: What exit is the Shasta Valley hummocks view?
alts: What exit is it for that?
Which exit for the lumpy hills?
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.a: It's exit 759. Look for small lumpy hills scattered across the flat valley floor.
ca759-the-hummocks-of-shasta-valley.quote: Look for small lumpy hills scattered across the flat valley floor.

ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.q: What is the biggest crop grown in Hay and cattle country?
alts: What do they grow in those fields?
What are all those fields growing, mom?
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.a: Alfalfa hay is the biggest field crop in Siskiyou County. In 2023, farmers cut about 175,000 tons of it from some 29,000 acres.
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.quote: Alfalfa hay is the county's biggest field crop: in 2023, farmers cut about 175,000 tons of it from some 29,000 acres.

ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.q: How many cattle live in Hay and cattle country?
alts: How many cows are out there?
Are those a lot of cows, dad?
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.a: Ranchers counted around 45,000 cattle and calves at the start of 2023.
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.quote: Ranchers counted around 45,000 cattle and calves at the start of that year.

ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.q: Why do the farms in Hay and cattle country need irrigation?
alts: Why does it need so much watering?
Why don't the fields just get rain, dad?
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.a: The valley sits in the rain shadow of the Klamath Mountains and gets only about 14 inches of rain a year, so the fields depend on groundwater and irrigation.
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.quote: The valley lies in the rain shadow of the Klamath Mountains and gets only about 14 inches of rain a year, so its fields depend on groundwater and irrigation.

ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.q: How much are the cattle in Hay and cattle country worth?
alts: How much money is all that cattle worth?
Are the cows worth a lot of money, dad?
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.a: In 2023, Siskiyou County's cows, steers, heifers and bulls together were worth about 112 million dollars.
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.quote: In 2023, its cows, steers, heifers and bulls together were worth about 112 million dollars.

ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.q: What did people do here before ranching in Hay and cattle country?
alts: Who lived here before the ranchers?
Did people live here a long time ago, mom?
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.a: Shasta people harvested grasshoppers here. They set patches of grassland on fire and gathered the cooked insects.
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.quote: Long before ranching, Shasta people here harvested grasshoppers by setting patches of grassland on fire and gathering the cooked insects.

ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.q: What else do farmers grow near Hay and cattle country?
alts: Do they grow anything besides hay?
Do they grow weird stuff here too, dad?
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.a: Siskiyou County also grows wheat, barley, rye and even mint.
ca762-hay-and-cattle-country.quote: The county also grows wheat, barley, rye and even mint.

ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.q: Do they really grow a billion strawberry plants in Siskiyou County?
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.a: Roughly, yes. In 2023 the county grew them on more than 2,800 acres, at about 360,000 plants per acre.
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.quote: In 2023 the county grew them on more than 2,800 acres, at about 360,000 plants per acre. That adds up to roughly a billion young plants

ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.q: Are the strawberry plants grown for berries we can eat?
alts: Do we eat what they grow?
Are those strawberries for eating or what?
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.a: No. They count as nursery crops, grown for planting rather than for berries.
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.quote: They count as nursery crops, grown for planting rather than for berries.

ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.q: How much money do the strawberry plants make for the county?
alts: How many dollars do all those plants bring in?
Is it a lot of money?
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.a: About 184 million dollars. That beats hay and cattle as the county's most valuable farm product.
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.quote: That adds up to roughly a billion young plants, worth about 184 million dollars.

ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.q: What else do farmers grow around Siskiyou County besides strawberry plants?
alts: What other stuff do kids see growing here?
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.a: The county also grew raspberry plants and garlic for planting. Farmers harvested about 3,300 acres of potatoes, including organic ones, and 170 acres of horseradish.
ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.quote: The county also grew raspberry plants and garlic for planting. Its farmers harvested about 3,300 acres of potatoes, including organic ones, and 170 acres of horseradish.

ca764-a-billion-strawberry-plants.q: What exit is the billion strawberry plants area at?
alts: Which exit do we take for the strawberry plants?

ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.q: How big is Shasta Valley Wildlife Area?
alts: How much land is that, mom?
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.a: It protects some 4,700 acres of juniper woodland, riverside forest, wetlands and fields, with Mount Shasta as its backdrop.
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.quote: protects some 4,700 acres of juniper woodland, riverside forest, wetlands and fields, with Mount Shasta as its backdrop

ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.q: When was Shasta Valley Wildlife Area set aside?
alts: Dad, when did this place start?
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.a: The wildlife area was set aside in 1991.
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.quote: The wildlife area was set aside in 1991.

ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.q: What birds can we see at Shasta Valley Wildlife Area?
alts: Are there any big birds there, dad?
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.a: Sandhill cranes, waterfowl, birds of prey and shorebirds all use it.
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.quote: Sandhill cranes, waterfowl, birds of prey and shorebirds all use it.

ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.q: What animals live at Shasta Valley Wildlife Area?
alts: Can we see deer or coyotes, mom?
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.a: Besides the birds, deer, porcupines and coyotes live there too.
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.quote: Deer, porcupines and coyotes live here too.

ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.q: Can you fish at Shasta Valley Wildlife Area?
alts: Can we catch fish there, dad?
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.a: Yes, it has three deep-water reservoirs, including Trout Lake, a trophy fishery for rainbow trout and largemouth bass.
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.quote: three deep-water reservoirs, including Trout Lake, a trophy fishery for rainbow trout and largemouth bass

ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.q: What should we know before visiting Shasta Valley Wildlife Area?
alts: Can we just go in anytime?
Is it okay to go there, mom?
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.a: During waterfowl hunting season, other visitors can come only on certain days, so it is worth checking before a visit.
ca766-shasta-valley-wildlife-area.quote: During waterfowl hunting season, other visitors can come only on certain days, so it is worth checking before a visit.

ca770-state-of-jefferson.q: What was the State of Jefferson?
alts: Was Jefferson a real state, or what?
ca770-state-of-jefferson.a: It was a 1941 plan to break away and form a new state from Siskiyou, Del Norte and Modoc counties in California plus four counties in Oregon.
ca770-state-of-jefferson.quote: The plan joined Siskiyou, Del Norte and Modoc counties in California with four counties in Oregon

ca770-state-of-jefferson.q: What happened on the day the State of Jefferson started?
alts: What did they do that day?
Did people really point guns at cars?
What went down on the highway?
ca770-state-of-jefferson.a: On November 27, 1941, young men waving hunting rifles stopped traffic on U.S. 99 south of Yreka and handed out a proclamation of independence for the State of Jefferson.
ca770-state-of-jefferson.quote: young men waving hunting rifles stopped traffic on U.S. 99 south of Yreka and handed out a proclamation of independence for the State of Jefferson

ca770-state-of-jefferson.q: What is the Double Cross on the State of Jefferson seal?
alts: Why is the seal a gold pan with Xs, Mom?
ca770-state-of-jefferson.a: The seal is a gold pan with two Xs, called the Double Cross. It stands for feeling abandoned by both state capitals.
ca770-state-of-jefferson.quote: The movement's seal is a gold pan with two Xs, called the Double Cross, for feeling abandoned by both state capitals.

ca770-state-of-jefferson.q: Who led the State of Jefferson movement and what happened to him?
alts: Who was in charge of it?
Who was the boss of Jefferson?
ca770-state-of-jefferson.a: Port Orford mayor Gilbert Gable led the movement. He died suddenly on December 2, 1941, and Yreka had been picked as the capital.
ca770-state-of-jefferson.quote: The movement's leader, Port Orford mayor Gilbert Gable, died suddenly on December 2, 1941.

ca770-state-of-jefferson.q: Why did the State of Jefferson rebellion fizzle out?
alts: Why didn't they get their own state?
ca770-state-of-jefferson.a: Five days after the leader died, Pearl Harbor was attacked, and people turned their attention to the war.
ca770-state-of-jefferson.quote: Five days later came Pearl Harbor, and the rebellion fizzled as people turned to the war.

ca770-state-of-jefferson.q: Where can we see the original State of Jefferson gold pan?
alts: Is the gold pan on display anywhere?
ca770-state-of-jefferson.a: The gold pan said to be the first model for the seal is on display at the Siskiyou County Museum in Yreka.
ca770-state-of-jefferson.quote: The gold pan said to be the first model for the seal is on display at the Siskiyou County Museum in Yreka.

ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.q: How did Yreka get its gold rush start?
alts: Why did people rush to Yreka, Dad?
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.a: A mule packer named Abraham Thompson found gold here in March 1851. By April, 2,000 miners had arrived at what they called Thompson's Dry Diggings.
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.quote: In March 1851, a mule packer named Abraham Thompson found gold here, and by April, 2,000 miners had arrived at what they called Thompson's Dry Diggings.

ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.q: Where does the name Yreka come from?
alts: Where does that name come from?
Why is it called Yreka, such a weird name?
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.a: It comes from waik'a, the Shasta people's word for Mount Shasta. In the Shasta language, waik'a means north mountain or white mountain.
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.quote: The name Yreka comes from waik'a, the Shasta people's word for Mount Shasta.

ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.q: What is Mark Twain's story about the name Yreka?
alts: What was that funny story about it?
Did a bakery sign really name Yreka?
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.a: Mark Twain told a funnier story: a bakery sign seen backwards, BAKERY without the B, read YREKA.
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.quote: Mark Twain told a funnier story: a bakery sign seen backwards, BAKERY without the B, read YREKA.

ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.q: What is the old courthouse in Yreka?
alts: What is that brick building about?
Is the courthouse still used, Mom?
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.a: Yreka is the county seat, and its brick courthouse was finished in 1857. It stayed in use until 2021.
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.quote: Yreka is the county seat, and its brick courthouse, finished in 1857, stayed in use until 2021.

ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.q: What is there to see in downtown Yreka?
alts: What can we see in it?
Is there anything cool to look at there?
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.a: The heart of downtown, along West Miner Street, is a historic district and a California Historical Landmark. The town also holds Gold Rush Days every June.
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.quote: The heart of downtown, along West Miner Street, is a historic district and a California Historical Landmark.

ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.q: What is the Karuk name for Yreka?
alts: What do the Karuk call it?
Is there another name for Yreka?
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.a: In the Karuk language, Yreka is kahtishraam. The Karuk Tribe has housing, offices and the Rain Rock Casino on its land here.
ca773-yreka-the-gold-town.quote: in the Karuk language Yreka is kahtishraam.

ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.q: Why did Yreka build its own railroad?
alts: Why did it have to build its own railroad?
Why didn't the train just come to Yreka?
Why'd Yreka make its own train?
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.a: The Southern Pacific skipped Yreka for a shorter, more level route through Montague. So the people of Yreka built their own railroad.
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.quote: it skipped Yreka for a shorter, more level route through Montague. So the people of Yreka built their own railroad.

ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.q: When did the Yreka Railroad open?
alts: When did the little train start?
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.a: The Yreka Railroad opened in January 1889. It connected the town to the main line at Montague.
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.quote: The Yreka Railroad opened in January 1889 and connected the town to the main line at Montague.

ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.q: Who bought the Yreka Western Railroad in 1953?
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.a: Willis Kyle bought it in 1953. He went on to build a group of short-line railroads.
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.quote: in 1953 it was bought by Willis Kyle, who went on to build a group of short-line railroads.

ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.q: Is the Yreka railroad still running today?
alts: Do trains still run on it?
Does the little train still go?
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.a: Yes, it still hauls freight such as wood chips, forest products and propane. Its tourist excursions ran for years, until 2016.
ca776-yreka-builds-its-own-railroad.quote: For years it also ran tourist excursions, until 2016. Today it still hauls freight such as wood chips, forest products and propane.

ca779-the-shasta-river.q: Where does the Shasta River start and where does it end up?
alts: Where does it start and finish?
Where does the river begin, Dad?
ca779-the-shasta-river.a: The Shasta River starts on Mount Eddy and runs 58 miles through Shasta Valley to the Klamath.
ca779-the-shasta-river.quote: The Shasta River starts on Mount Eddy and runs 58 miles through Shasta Valley to the Klamath.

ca779-the-shasta-river.q: Where does the Shasta River get its water?
alts: Where does it get its water from?
Is the river water from the mountain?
ca779-the-shasta-river.a: Most of it comes from groundwater and irrigation runoff. Some is Mount Shasta snowmelt that flows out of lava tubes as springs.
ca779-the-shasta-river.quote: Most of its water comes from groundwater and irrigation runoff, and some is Mount Shasta snowmelt that flows out of lava tubes as springs

ca779-the-shasta-river.q: Do salmon still return to the Shasta River today?
alts: Are there still salmon in it?
Are there still lots of fish there?
ca779-the-shasta-river.a: Yes, but far fewer. Today fewer than one in ten of those salmon still return, and recent droughts have made it hard for young fish to survive.
ca779-the-shasta-river.quote: Today fewer than one in ten of those salmon still return, and recent droughts have made it hard for young fish to survive.

ca779-the-shasta-river.q: What kinds of fish live in the Shasta River?
alts: What animals live in the river?
ca779-the-shasta-river.a: Chinook salmon spawn there, and the river also supports coho salmon and steelhead.
ca779-the-shasta-river.quote: The river also supports coho salmon and steelhead.

ca781-the-shasta-people.q: Where is the homeland of the Shasta people?
alts: Where did the Shasta people live, mom?
ca781-the-shasta-people.a: Shasta Valley and the nearby Klamath River are part of the Shasta homeland. The people of the Shasta River were known as the Ahotireitsu.
ca781-the-shasta-people.quote: Shasta Valley and the nearby Klamath River are part of the homeland of the Shasta people, and the people of the Shasta River were known as the Ahotireitsu.

ca781-the-shasta-people.q: What did Shasta children do along the Klamath River?
alts: Did they do that as kids too?
What did Shasta kids do for fun or food?
ca781-the-shasta-people.a: Women and children dove in the Klamath River for mussels.
ca781-the-shasta-people.quote: Women and children dove in the Klamath for mussels.

ca781-the-shasta-people.q: Do Shasta people still live here today?
alts: Are there still Shasta people, or did they all go away?
ca781-the-shasta-people.a: Yes. Today Shasta people live in Yreka and on the Quartz Valley Indian Reservation, and on the Grand Ronde and Siletz reservations in Oregon.
ca781-the-shasta-people.quote: Today Shasta people live in Yreka and on the Quartz Valley Indian Reservation, and on the Grand Ronde and Siletz reservations in Oregon.

ca781-the-shasta-people.q: What happened to the Shasta people during the Gold Rush?
alts: What did that do to them?
Why did the miners hurt the Shasta people?
ca781-the-shasta-people.a: Gold miners poured onto Shasta land in 1850 and 1851. In July 1852, miners killed 14 Shasta people in Shasta Valley, and in the late 1850s families were forcibly removed to reservations in Oregon.
ca781-the-shasta-people.quote: In July 1852, miners killed 14 Shasta people in Shasta Valley in revenge for the death of a white man.

ca781-the-shasta-people.q: What was the Shasta treaty of 1851?
alts: Did the Shasta get promised land and then not get it?
ca781-the-shasta-people.a: Shasta leaders signed a treaty in November 1851 promising a reservation in Scott Valley. It was one of 18 California treaties the state opposed and the U.S. Senate rejected.
ca781-the-shasta-people.quote: In November 1851, Shasta leaders signed a treaty that promised them a reservation in Scott Valley, but it was one of 18 California treaties that the state opposed and the U.S. Senate rejected.

ca783-the-klamath-mountains.q: How did the Klamath Mountains form?
alts: How'd these mountains get here, anyway?
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.a: Their rocks began as volcanic islands and pieces of other continents in the Pacific. They later crashed into North America.
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.quote: Their rocks began as volcanic islands and pieces of other continents out in the Pacific

ca783-the-klamath-mountains.q: What trees grow in the Klamath Mountains?
alts: What kind of trees are in there?
What are all those trees on the mountains?
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.a: They hold one of the richest mixes of cone-bearing trees on Earth, about 30 kinds. Brewer's spruce and Port Orford cedar grow almost nowhere else.
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.quote: They hold one of the richest mixes of cone-bearing trees on Earth, about 30 kinds.

ca783-the-klamath-mountains.q: What is the Miracle Mile in the Klamath Mountains?
alts: What was that Miracle Mile thing?
Why is it called a miracle?
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.a: It's a single square mile of the Russian Wilderness where botanists counted 17 kinds of conifers in 1969. An 18th was found there in 2013.
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.quote: In 1969, botanists counted 17 kinds of conifers in a single square mile of the Russian Wilderness and called it the Miracle Mile.

ca783-the-klamath-mountains.q: What animals live in the Klamath Mountains?
alts: Are there bears in those mountains?
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.a: The mountains hold black bears and mountain lions. They also hold nine native species in the salmon family.
ca783-the-klamath-mountains.quote: The mountains also hold serpentine and marble, black bears and mountain lions, and nine native species in the salmon family.

alts: Who is this rest area named after, anyway?
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.a: He was a California State Senator who lived in Siskiyou County nearly all his life. This rest area by the Klamath River honors him.
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.quote: This rest area by the Klamath River honors State Senator Randolph Collier, who lived in Siskiyou County nearly all his life.

ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.q: What is Randolph Collier famous for?
alts: What did he do that was so important?
Why did they name a rest area after him?
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.a: He co-wrote the 1947 law that laid the groundwork for California's freeway system. So in a way, you're driving on his idea.
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.quote: He co-wrote the 1947 law that laid the groundwork for California's freeway system, so in a way, you're driving on his idea.

ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.q: How long was Randolph Collier a state senator?
alts: How long was he in the Senate?
How many years did he work for the state?
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.a: He served in the California state Senate from 1939 to 1976, and he chaired its Transportation Committee.
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.quote: Collier served in the state Senate from 1939 to 1976 and chaired its Transportation Committee.

ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.q: What did Randolph Collier have to do with Highway 99?
alts: Did he have something to do with it ending?
Why did old Highway 99 go away?
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.a: In 1963, his bill to simplify California's highway numbers began the end of U.S. 99.
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.quote: In 1963, his bill to simplify California's highway numbers began the end of U.S. 99.

ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.q: What is the Randolph Collier Rest Area exit number?
alts: What exit do we take for it?
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.a: It's at exit 786, and the rest area is just 0.1 miles off the freeway.

ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.q: What else is named after Randolph Collier?
alts: Is anything else named after him?
Is there anything else with his name on it?
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.a: A tunnel on U.S. 199, the Redwood Highway, also carries his name.
ca786-randolph-collier-rest-area.quote: A tunnel on U.S. 199, the Redwood Highway, also carries his name.

ca786-the-klamath-river.q: What happened to the dams on the Klamath River?
alts: What happened to the dams on it?
Did they really knock down dams here?
ca786-the-klamath-river.a: Four hydroelectric dams upstream were torn down in 2023 and 2024. It was the largest dam removal in American history.
ca786-the-klamath-river.quote: Upstream, four hydroelectric dams were torn down in 2023 and 2024, the largest dam removal in American history.

ca786-the-klamath-river.q: Why does the Klamath River matter for salmon?
alts: Why does it matter for fish?
Are there lots of fish in this river?
ca786-the-klamath-river.a: The Klamath is the third-largest salmon and steelhead river on the West Coast of the lower 48 states.
ca786-the-klamath-river.quote: The Klamath is the third-largest salmon and steelhead river on the West Coast of the lower 48 states.

ca786-the-klamath-river.q: Have salmon come back to the Klamath River since the dams came down?
