alts: Did the fish come back after that?
Did any salmon swim up the river?
ca786-the-klamath-river.a: Yes. On October 17, 2024, a fall-run Chinook salmon was spotted in Oregon's Upper Klamath Basin, the first to reach it in more than 100 years.
ca786-the-klamath-river.quote: On October 17, 2024, a fall-run Chinook salmon was spotted in Oregon's Upper Klamath Basin, the first to reach it in more than 100 years.

ca786-the-klamath-river.q: How much river did removing the Klamath dams open up?
alts: How much river did that open up?
How far can the fish go now?
Is it a lot of river?
ca786-the-klamath-river.a: Removing the dams reopened about 400 miles of river to spawning salmon. Copco No. 2 came down first, in October 2023, and the last dam was gone in 2024.
ca786-the-klamath-river.quote: Copco No. 2 came down first, in October 2023, and the last of the dams was gone in 2024, reopening about 400 miles of river to spawning salmon.

ca786-the-klamath-river.q: How do I spot the Klamath River from I-5?
alts: How do we spot it from the freeway?
Where do we look to see the river?
ca786-the-klamath-river.a: Look for the river below the freeway bridge. It's near Exit 786, where the river turns sharply south to meet I-5.
ca786-the-klamath-river.quote: The freeway crosses the Klamath River near here, where the river turns sharply south to meet I-5.

ca787-into-karuk-country.q: What does the word Karuk mean?
alts: Why are they called the Karuk, Mom?
ca787-into-karuk-country.a: Karuk means upriver. Traditionally the Karuk also called themselves the middle of the world people.
ca787-into-karuk-country.quote: Karuk means upriver, and traditionally the Karuk called themselves the middle of the world people.

ca787-into-karuk-country.q: How many Karuk people are there?
alts: How many people are in that tribe?
Are there a lot of Karuk people?
ca787-into-karuk-country.a: The Karuk Tribe is one of the largest tribes in California. The 2010 census counted about 6,100 Karuk people.
ca787-into-karuk-country.quote: The Karuk Tribe is one of the largest tribes in California, and the 2010 census counted about 6,100 Karuk people.

ca787-into-karuk-country.q: How much land is Karuk ancestral territory?
alts: Is that a lot of land, Dad?
ca787-into-karuk-country.a: Karuk ancestral territory covers more than a million acres along the Klamath. It's land the tribe has never ceded.
ca787-into-karuk-country.quote: Karuk ancestral territory covers more than a million acres along the Klamath, land the tribe has never ceded.

ca787-into-karuk-country.q: What was the Klamath River like for the Karuk long ago?
alts: What used to be along that river?
Did people live along the river, Mom?
ca787-into-karuk-country.a: The river was once lined with more than 120 Karuk villages. Highway 96 follows the Klamath River west into Karuk country.
ca787-into-karuk-country.quote: The river was once lined with more than 120 Karuk villages.

ca787-into-karuk-country.q: What does the Karuk Tribe do today?
alts: Is the tribe still around, Dad?
ca787-into-karuk-country.a: The tribe serves its people from Happy Camp, Orleans and Yreka. It runs everything from health clinics to salmon restoration, cultural burning and dam removal work.
ca787-into-karuk-country.quote: Today the tribe serves its people from Happy Camp, Orleans and Yreka, and runs everything from health clinics to salmon restoration, cultural burning and dam removal work.

ca787-into-karuk-country.q: Is the Karuk language still spoken?
alts: Can they still talk Karuk, Mom?
ca787-into-karuk-country.a: The Karuk language is not related to any other known language. Fewer than five people spoke it fluently full-time as of 2025, and the tribe has an active program to bring it back.
ca787-into-karuk-country.quote: Fewer than five people spoke it fluently full-time as of 2025, and the tribe has an active program to bring it back.

ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.q: Where did the name Siskiyou come from?
alts: Where did it get that name?
Why is it called Siskiyou, anyway?
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.a: Nobody is sure. One story says it was a Cree word for a bob-tailed horse. Another says it comes from the French name Six Cailloux, meaning six stones.
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.quote: Nobody is sure where the name Siskiyou comes from. One story says it was a Cree word for a bob-tailed horse.

alts: Does Siskiyou mean something silly, like a horse?
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.a: It might mean bob-tailed horse, from a Cree word, or six stones, from the French Six Cailloux. Nobody knows for sure which story is right.
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.quote: Hudson's Bay Company trappers gave a river ford the French name Six Cailloux, six stones

ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.q: What is the bob-tailed horse story behind Siskiyou?
alts: Was there really a horse named Siskiyou?
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.a: Historian Richard Mackie says a bob-tailed horse died in 1829 on Alexander McLeod's Hudson's Bay Company trip over a pass. The pass was later named for it.
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.quote: a bob-tailed horse died in 1829 on Alexander McLeod's Hudson's Bay Company trip over a pass that was later named for it.

ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.q: What is the six stones story about the Siskiyou name?
alts: What are the six rocks the name is about?
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.a: The ford was on Oregon's Umpqua River, where six large rocks lay in the water. Trapper Stephen Meek is said to have carried the name to the Klamath.
ca789-where-siskiyou-got-its-name.quote: That ford was on Oregon's Umpqua River, where six large rocks lay in the water, and trapper Stephen Meek is said to have carried the name to the Klamath.

ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.q: Why does Hornbrook have an agricultural inspection station?
alts: Why do we have to stop at that station?
Why are we stopping here, is somebody checking us?
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.a: Inspectors here look for pests in plants or cargo that could harm California's farms. It's one of 16 stations the state runs where major highways cross into California.
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.quote: Inspectors look for pests in plants or cargo that could harm California's farms.

ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.q: What will the inspectors ask us at the Hornbrook station?
alts: Do they check passenger cars like ours?
Are they going to search our car, Mom?
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.a: Passenger cars with California or neighboring-state plates usually get just a few questions about what they're carrying. RVs, trucks, and vehicles hauling boats or livestock are higher risk, and their loads may be looked over.
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.quote: Passenger cars with California or neighboring-state plates usually get just a few questions about what they carry.

ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.q: How old are the agricultural inspection stations?
alts: When did they start doing this at the border?
How long have they been checking cars, like a hundred years?
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.a: The first stations went up in the early 1920s on highways from Nevada near Reno. Destructive alfalfa weevils had turned up in campgrounds along those roads.
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.quote: The first stations went up in the early 1920s on highways from Nevada near Reno, after destructive alfalfa weevils turned up in campgrounds along them

ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.q: What happened that led to the first inspection stations?
alts: What was the first bug they found?
Did they really find bugs in people's camping stuff?
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.a: Destructive alfalfa weevils turned up in campgrounds along highways from Nevada. In the first year, inspectors found live weevils inside camping gear.
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.quote: in the first year inspectors found live weevils inside camping gear.

ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.q: What happens with bees at the Hornbrook inspection station?
alts: Do they check trucks carrying beehives?
Do they check for bees, too?
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.a: Loads of beehives are logged, and the driver must name where in California the bees are going. That way the county's agriculture office can inspect them on arrival.
ca790-agricultural-inspection-at-hornbro.quote: Loads of beehives are logged, and the driver must name where in California the bees are going, so that county's agriculture office can inspect them on arrival.

ca796-hilt-the-border-town.q: Why is the town called Hilt?
alts: Why's it got such a weird name, Mom?
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.a: Hilt is named for an early settler, John Hilt.
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.quote: It's named for an early settler, John Hilt.

ca796-hilt-the-border-town.q: What kind of town is Hilt?
alts: What was that town built for?
Why did people even live there?
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.a: Hilt grew up as a company town, first for the Northern California Lumber Company and then for the Fruit Growers Supply Company, an affiliate of Sunkist.
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.quote: It grew up as a company town, first for the Northern California Lumber Company and then for the Fruit Growers Supply Company, an affiliate of Sunkist.

alts: Which exit do we take for it?
Is that the last exit in California?
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.a: Hilt is exit 796, the northernmost I-5 exit in California.
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.quote: Hilt has the northernmost I-5 exit in California.

ca796-hilt-the-border-town.q: What happened to Hilt in the Klamathon Fire?
alts: Was there a big fire there?
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.a: In July 2018 the Klamathon Fire forced Hilt to evacuate. It destroyed 82 structures and killed one person before it was contained on July 21.
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.quote: It destroyed 82 structures and killed one person before it was contained on July 21.

ca796-hilt-the-border-town.q: What started the Klamathon Fire near Hilt?
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.a: The fire started near Hornbrook, and investigators blamed reckless burning of debris.
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.quote: Investigators blamed reckless burning of debris.

ca796-hilt-the-border-town.q: What mountains are just north of Hilt?
alts: What are those mountains past it?
What's up the road from the town?
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.a: The Siskiyou Mountains rise just north of Hilt. They are the divide between the Klamath and Rogue river basins.
ca796-hilt-the-border-town.quote: Just north of Hilt rise the Siskiyou Mountains, the divide between the Klamath and Rogue river basins.

alts: What is that line we're crossing?
Why is there a line on the map here?
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.a: It's the line the California and Oregon border follows. It was set in an 1819 treaty between the United States and Spain.
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.quote: The California and Oregon border follows the 42nd parallel, a line set in an 1819 treaty between the United States and Spain.

ca797-the-42nd-parallel.q: Why is the California border at the 42nd parallel?
alts: Why did California use that line?
Why is the border here, Mom?
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.a: California kept the line from the 1819 treaty. When it became a state in 1850, it kept that line as its northern border.
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.quote: When California became a state in 1850, it kept that line as its northern border.

ca797-the-42nd-parallel.q: Is there a border dispute at the 42nd parallel?
alts: Did people fight over the border?
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.a: Yes. A survey around 1870 marked the line with errors, creating a dispute that continues to this day.
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.quote: A survey around 1870 marked it with errors, creating a dispute that continues to this day.

ca797-the-42nd-parallel.q: How high does I-5 get near the 42nd parallel?
alts: How high is it up there?
Are we going up a mountain?
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.a: A few miles north, in Oregon, I-5 crosses Siskiyou Summit at 4,310 feet, its highest point anywhere.
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.quote: A few miles north, in Oregon, I-5 crosses Siskiyou Summit at 4,310 feet, its highest point anywhere.

ca797-the-42nd-parallel.q: What is Pilot Rock near the 42nd parallel?
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.a: Pilot Rock is a volcanic plug about 25 million years old, just east of the summit. It guided pioneers coming north from California on the Applegate Trail.
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.quote: Just east of the summit stands Pilot Rock, a volcanic plug about 25 million years old that guided pioneers coming north from California on the Applegate Trail.

ca797-the-42nd-parallel.q: Does the Pacific Crest Trail cross I-5 near the 42nd parallel?
alts: Can hikers cross the freeway up there?
Is there a hiking trail up there?
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.a: Yes. A few miles north at Siskiyou Summit, the Pacific Crest Trail crosses the freeway. Snow generally falls up there from November through April.
ca797-the-42nd-parallel.quote: The Pacific Crest Trail crosses the freeway up there, and snow generally falls from November through April.

z:0.q: Whose land is the Border and South Bay stretch on?
z:0.a: This stretch crosses Kumeyaay land, between the San Ysidro border crossing and Chula Vista.
z:0.quote: the freeway crosses Kumeyaay land of river valleys, salt ponds and marsh at the south end of San Diego Bay

z:0.q: What kind of land does I-5 cross near the South Bay?
alts: What kind of land is that out there?
z:0.a: The freeway crosses river valleys, salt ponds and marsh at the south end of San Diego Bay.
z:0.quote: the freeway crosses Kumeyaay land of river valleys, salt ponds and marsh at the south end of San Diego Bay

z:9.q: What do we pass along San Diego Bay and downtown?
alts: What all do we go through on this stretch?
What's along here, like what places?
z:9.a: This stretch follows the east side of the bay through National City, the Navy's piers, Barrio Logan, downtown, the airport and Old Town.
z:9.quote: This stretch follows the east side of San Diego Bay through National City, the Navy's piers, Barrio Logan, downtown, the airport and Old Town.

z:9.q: Why is San Diego often cool and gray in summer mornings?
alts: Why is it so gray here in the morning?
Why are there so many clouds near the coast?
z:9.a: Marine layer clouds, most common from May to August, often keep mornings near the coast cool and gray. Locals call it May gray and June gloom.
z:9.quote: Marine layer clouds, most common from May to August, often keep mornings near the coast cool and gray, a pattern locals call May gray and June gloom.

z:9.q: What is May gray and June gloom in San Diego?
alts: What do locals mean by June gloom?
What's May gray, can we ask about it?
z:9.a: It's the local name for marine layer clouds that often keep mornings near the coast cool and gray. They're most common from May to August.
z:9.quote: Marine layer clouds, most common from May to August, often keep mornings near the coast cool and gray, a pattern locals call May gray and June gloom.

z:9.q: When does San Diego get most of its rain?
alts: Does it rain much around here?
When does it rain here, kids want to know?
z:9.a: Most of the year's rain falls from December through March, and it totals less than 12 inches on average.
z:9.quote: Most of the year's rain, less than 12 inches on average, falls from December through March.

z:20.q: What is special about Mission Bay's islands?
alts: Why are the islands in Mission Bay weird?
Are the Mission Bay islands real?
z:20.a: Mission Bay's islands are man-made. They are one of the things that line this stretch of the road.
z:20.quote: Mission Bay's man-made islands, Rose Canyon and its fault, and the slopes of Mount Soledad line this stretch

z:20.q: What is Rose Canyon along this stretch?
alts: Is Rose Canyon a big deal?
z:20.a: Rose Canyon is one of the landmarks along this stretch, and it comes with a fault. The fault is named right along with the canyon.

z:20.q: Is there a fault near Rose Canyon?
alts: Mom, is there an earthquake line here?
z:20.a: Yes, the stretch is lined by Rose Canyon and its fault. That fault is one of the features of this part of the drive.

z:20.q: What is Mount Soledad on this drive?
alts: What's that hill beside the road?
What's the big hill we're passing?
z:20.a: Mount Soledad's slopes line this stretch of road between Mission Bay and La Jolla. They are one of the landmarks you pass.
z:20.quote: the slopes of Mount Soledad line this stretch

z:20.q: What can we see between Mission Bay and La Jolla?
alts: What's along this part of the drive?
What are we passing right now?
z:20.a: You pass Mission Bay's man-made islands, Rose Canyon and its fault, and the slopes of Mount Soledad. UC San Diego and University City are along this stretch too.
z:20.quote: Mission Bay's man-made islands, Rose Canyon and its fault, and the slopes of Mount Soledad line this stretch, along with UC San Diego and University City.

z:31.q: What are the lagoons we pass between Torrey Pines and Encinitas?
alts: What are those lagoons out there?
Mom, what's that watery stuff by the ocean?
z:31.a: They're coastal lagoons where creeks and rivers meet the sea. The three named here are Los Peñasquitos, San Dieguito and San Elijo.
z:31.quote: A string of coastal lagoons where creeks and rivers meet the sea, Los Peñasquitos, San Dieguito and San Elijo

z:31.q: Which beach towns are on this stretch of I-5?
alts: What towns are we passing, Dad?
z:31.a: This stretch alternates between the lagoons and the beach towns of Del Mar, Solana Beach and Encinitas.
z:31.quote: alternates with the beach towns of Del Mar, Solana Beach and Encinitas.

z:31.q: Is there another Del Mar race season besides summer?
alts: Do they race again later in the year?
Do the horses come back in the fall, Dad?
z:31.a: Yes, there's a second Del Mar race meet that runs in November.
z:31.quote: A second Del Mar race meet runs in November.

z:44.q: What kind of town is Oceanside?
z:44.a: Oceanside is a beach town. It fills part of this stretch of road along with Carlsbad's fields and lagoons.
z:44.quote: and the beach town of Oceanside fill this stretch of Luiseño and Kumeyaay country.

z:44.q: Whose land were Carlsbad and Oceanside originally?
z:44.a: This stretch of road runs through Luiseño and Kumeyaay country, so those are the peoples tied to this land.
z:44.quote: fill this stretch of Luiseño and Kumeyaay country.

z:44.q: Is there anything to do with the strawberry farm in fall?
z:44.a: Yes, the strawberry farm's pumpkin season picks up in late September, so fall brings pumpkins along with the berry fields.
z:44.quote: In fall: The strawberry farm's pumpkin season picks up in late September.

alts: What is that big base the freeway runs through?
Is this where the Marines live, Buddy?
z:54.a: It's Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton. The land along this stretch of the coast is kept for Marine training.
z:54.quote: Through Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton the freeway follows the ocean for about 18 miles

z:54.q: How long does I-5 follow the ocean through Camp Pendleton?
alts: How far does it stay along the water here?
Are we gonna see the ocean for a long time?
How long is this coastal part?
z:54.a: The freeway follows the ocean for about 18 miles through the base.
z:54.quote: the freeway follows the ocean for about 18 miles

z:54.q: What can we see along the Camp Pendleton coast?
alts: What is there to look at on this stretch?
What's out the window, Buddy? I'm bored!
z:54.a: You'll pass open hills, river valleys and the Surf Line railroad, all with the ocean beside you.
z:54.quote: past open hills, river valleys and the Surf Line railroad

z:70.q: What is Trestles near San Onofre?
alts: What is that surf spot by the freeway?
z:70.a: Trestles is a set of surf breaks at the north edge of Camp Pendleton. The freeway runs above San Onofre's beaches and the Trestles surf breaks.
z:70.quote: The freeway runs above San Onofre's beaches and the surf breaks of Trestles at the north edge of Camp Pendleton.

z:70.q: Where does Orange County start on this stretch?
alts: Where is it that we leave San Diego County?
Are we in Orange County yet?
z:70.a: The Orange County line is at Cristianitos Road, beside the hillside streets of Spanish-style San Clemente.
z:70.quote: The Orange County line is at Cristianitos Road, beside the hillside streets of Spanish-style San Clemente.

z:70.q: What happens at San Mateo Creek in winter?
alts: What does it do when storms come?
Why do fish swim up the creek?
z:70.a: Winter storms can push San Mateo Creek through the sandbar at its mouth. That lets steelhead trout swim upstream to spawn.
z:70.quote: Winter storms can push San Mateo Creek through the sandbar at its mouth, letting steelhead trout swim upstream to spawn.

z:70.q: Is there a stream at Trestles?
alts: Does it have water running through it?
Is there a little river at the surf spot?
z:70.a: Yes, usually in winter and spring. After heavy rains, a small seasonal stream usually runs through Trestles.
z:70.quote: After heavy rains, a small seasonal stream usually runs through Trestles in winter and spring.

z:76.q: Whose homeland is the Capistrano Valley?
alts: Who lived here first, like before everybody?
Who were the first people here?
z:76.a: The valley of San Juan and Trabuco creeks is Acjachemen homeland. The freeway runs inland through it between Dana Point and Mission Viejo.
z:76.quote: the freeway runs inland through the valley of San Juan and Trabuco creeks, Acjachemen homeland

z:76.q: What town are we passing near in Capistrano Valley?
alts: What town is this, is it a real mission?
z:76.a: We pass the mission town of San Juan Capistrano. The freeway runs by it as it heads inland through the valley.
z:76.quote: past the mission town of San Juan Capistrano

z:76.q: What is the ranch land out east of the freeway here?
alts: What's that land to the east?
Is that a farm out there?
z:76.a: To the east lie the ranch lands of Rancho Mission Viejo. They sit along the freeway as it runs through the valley.
z:76.quote: with the ranch lands of Rancho Mission Viejo to the east

z:76.q: When do the Capistrano swallows leave?
alts: When do the birds fly away?
z:76.a: Tradition says the swallows leave around October 23. That is the old feast day of Saint John of Capistrano.
z:76.quote: Tradition says the swallows leave around October 23, the old feast day of Saint John of Capistrano.

z:76.q: How much rain does the Capistrano Valley area get?
z:76.a: The area gets roughly 12 inches of rain a year. Almost all of it falls between November and March.
z:76.quote: Almost all of the area's roughly 12 inches of yearly rain falls between November and March.

z:86.q: What towns are in Saddleback Valley?
alts: What cities are down in this valley, Dad?
z:86.a: Suburbs of Mission Viejo, Laguna Hills and Lake Forest fill the Saddleback Valley, below the mountain's two peaks.
z:86.quote: Suburbs of Mission Viejo, Laguna Hills and Lake Forest fill the Saddleback Valley below the mountain's two peaks

z:86.q: What is the El Toro Y near Saddleback Valley?
alts: What's the El Toro Y, Mom?
z:86.a: It's where Interstate 405 meets this freeway, in the Saddleback Valley area.
z:86.quote: Interstate 405 meets this freeway at the El Toro Y.

z:86.q: Does it ever snow on Saddleback?
alts: Does it snow on that mountain?
Is there ever snow up on those peaks?
z:86.a: Yes, a little. During most winters, snow dusts Santiago Peak, the higher summit of Saddleback, at least once.
z:86.quote: During most winters, snow dusts Santiago Peak, the higher summit of Saddleback, at least once.

z:86.q: Which peak is the highest on Saddleback?
alts: What's the tallest part of that mountain?
z:86.a: Santiago Peak is the higher summit of Saddleback. The mountain has two peaks in all.
z:86.quote: snow dusts Santiago Peak, the higher summit of Saddleback

z:86.q: What are the Santa Ana winds around Saddleback Valley?
alts: Why are the hills so dangerous in fall?
z:86.a: Autumn is the season known for hot, dry Santa Ana winds. They create critical fire weather in the hills.
z:86.quote: Autumn is the season known for hot, dry Santa Ana winds, which create critical fire weather in the hills.

alts: What was that ranch we're crossing?
Is this land a ranch, Dad?
z:95.a: It's the old ranch land the freeway crosses here. The land is flat, and the stretch is named for it, the old Irvine Ranch.
z:95.quote: The freeway crosses the flat land of the old Irvine Ranch and passes Tustin's old Marine base.

z:95.q: What is special about the land around Irvine Ranch?
alts: What's the land like around it?
Why is everything so flat here?
z:95.a: The land here is flat. The freeway crosses the flat land of the old Irvine Ranch.
z:95.quote: The freeway crosses the flat land of the old Irvine Ranch and passes Tustin's old Marine base.

z:95.q: What will we see driving past Tustin?
alts: What is there to see along here?
z:95.a: You'll cross the flat land of the old Irvine Ranch and pass Tustin's old Marine base. It's a stretch to watch the landscape and spot that old base.
z:95.quote: The freeway crosses the flat land of the old Irvine Ranch and passes Tustin's old Marine base.

z:95.q: Why is the morning so gray in Tustin and Irvine Ranch?
alts: Why is it so cloudy in the morning?
Why is the sky gray, Dad?
z:95.a: In late spring and early summer it's June Gloom. Mornings are overcast, with occasional drizzle.
z:95.quote: Late spring and early summer bring June Gloom, with overcast mornings and occasional drizzle.

z:103.q: What famous places does I-5 pass in Santa Ana and Anaheim?
alts: What famous stuff is near it?
Are we going to see anything cool, like Disneyland?
z:103.a: The freeway passes Christ Cathedral and Disneyland. It also crosses the Santa Ana River and the Orange Crush interchange.
z:103.quote: The freeway crosses the Santa Ana River and the Orange Crush interchange and passes Christ Cathedral and Disneyland

z:103.q: What is the Santa Ana River like?
alts: Does it always have a lot of water in it?
Is that a real river, it looks dry?
z:103.a: It carries only a small flow most of the year. In the brief winter rainy season it can get flash floods.
z:103.quote: The Santa Ana River carries only a small flow except in the brief winter rainy season, when it is prone to flash floods.

z:103.q: What are the Santa Ana winds?
alts: Why is it so hot and windy in the fall?
z:103.a: They bring hot, dry weather in the fall. Their wind damage is most common along the Santa Ana River basin.
z:103.quote: Santa Ana winds bring hot, dry autumn weather, and their wind damage is most common along the Santa Ana River basin.

z:112.q: What counties does I-5 cross between Buena Park and Norwalk?
alts: Does it go from one county to another here?
Are we leaving Orange County yet?
z:112.a: Between Buena Park and Downey, the freeway crosses the line between Orange and Los Angeles counties.
z:112.quote: Between Buena Park and Downey the freeway crosses the line between Orange and Los Angeles counties

z:112.q: What are the Gateway Cities along this part of I-5?
alts: Which cities is it running through here?
z:112.a: The freeway runs through the Gateway Cities of La Mirada, Santa Fe Springs and Norwalk.
z:112.quote: runs through the Gateway Cities of La Mirada, Santa Fe Springs and Norwalk

z:112.q: What did people grow or raise on this land in the past?
alts: Did they have cows or something here?
z:112.a: The land later held olive groves and dairies, and it also had oil fields.
z:112.quote: later held olive groves, dairies and oil fields

z:124.q: What rivers does I-5 cross around Downey and Commerce?
alts: What rivers does it cross here?
Are we going over any rivers, like real ones?
z:124.a: Through this stretch the freeway crosses the San Gabriel River and the Rio Hondo, on its way through Downey, Commerce and East Los Angeles.
z:124.quote: The freeway crosses the San Gabriel River and the Rio Hondo

z:124.q: What is Downey known for along I-5?
alts: Why do they call Downey the aerospace place, what's that mean?
z:124.a: Downey is described as an aerospace town. The freeway runs right through it, so this is aerospace country.
z:124.quote: runs through aerospace Downey, the rail-side factories of Commerce, and East Los Angeles

z:124.q: What is Commerce like along the freeway?
alts: Are there lots of factories, like in a big factory city?
z:124.a: Commerce is a place of rail-side factories. The freeway passes right through that industrial area on the way to East Los Angeles.

z:124.q: What places does I-5 run through between Downey and East LA?
alts: What places does it go through?
What towns are we driving through next?
z:124.a: The freeway runs through aerospace Downey, then the rail-side factories of Commerce, and then East Los Angeles.
z:124.quote: runs through aerospace Downey, the rail-side factories of Commerce, and East Los Angeles

z:134.q: What is Lincoln Heights along this stretch of I-5?
alts: What's that neighborhood the freeway runs through?
What's Lincoln Heights, is it a big deal?
z:134.a: Lincoln Heights is described as the city's first suburb. The freeway runs right through it between Boyle Heights and Elysian Park.
z:134.quote: runs through Lincoln Heights, the city's first suburb

z:134.q: What river does I-5 cross near Elysian Park?
alts: What river is it that we cross there?
Are we going over a river, what's it called?
