alts: Did people dig for gold along it?
Were there real gold miners here, like in the movies?
z:704.a: Yes, the freeway runs past old Gold Rush camps in the canyon, along with old stage stops.
z:704.quote: past old stage stops and Gold Rush camps

z:704.q: Does it snow in the Sacramento River canyon north of Redding?
alts: Could we get snow up there?
Will there be snow on the road up ahead?
z:704.a: Yes, snow can fall at higher elevations north of Redding from fall to spring, and Caltrans sometimes requires chains.
z:704.quote: North of Redding, snow can fall at higher elevations from fall to spring, and Caltrans sometimes requires chains.

z:722.q: What kind of town is Dunsmuir?
alts: What's it like down in that canyon?
Is Dunsmuir an old town, Mom?
z:722.a: Dunsmuir is an old railroad town. It fills the bottom of the canyon, with granite spires rising above it.
z:722.quote: Granite spires rise west of the freeway, and an old railroad town fills the canyon bottom.

z:722.q: How much rain and snow does Dunsmuir get?
alts: Does it get a lot of snow there?
Is it super snowy in Dunsmuir?
z:722.a: Dunsmuir gets about 63 inches of rain and snow a year. That's about three and a half times as much as Yreka or Medford.
z:722.quote: Dunsmuir gets about 63 inches of rain and snow a year, about three and a half times as much as Yreka or Medford.

z:722.q: When does Dunsmuir get most of its rain and snow?
alts: When does it snow in Dunsmuir?
z:722.a: More than half of Dunsmuir's yearly rain and snow falls in just three months: December, January and February.
z:722.quote: More than half of Dunsmuir's yearly rain and snow falls in December, January and February.

z:722.q: Are there fish to catch in Dunsmuir?
alts: Can people fish in that river?
Are there big fish in the river?
z:722.a: Yes. In summer, Dunsmuir stocks the river in town with trophy rainbow trout up to 14 pounds.
z:722.quote: In summer, Dunsmuir stocks the river in town with trophy rainbow trout up to 14 pounds.

z:722.q: When does it start freezing in Dunsmuir?
alts: When is the first frost there?
When does the freezing stop in spring?
z:722.a: The first freeze usually arrives around October 20. In an average year, the last freeze comes around April 24.
z:722.quote: The first freeze usually arrives around October 20.

z:735.q: What is Black Butte near Mount Shasta?
alts: What is that dark cone over there?
What's that black hill, is it a volcano too?
z:735.a: Black Butte is the dark cone you see near Mount Shasta. It stands close to the foot of the volcano, along with the city of Mount Shasta and Black Butte Summit.
z:735.quote: the city of Mount Shasta, the dark cone of Black Butte and Black Butte Summit.

z:735.q: What record did Mount Shasta set for snow?
alts: What happened with the snow on it in 1959?
How much snow did it get, was it a lot?
z:735.a: In February 1959 the old Ski Bowl on Mount Shasta got 15.75 feet of snow in one storm. That is a U.S. record.
z:735.quote: In February 1959 the old Ski Bowl on Mount Shasta got 15.75 feet of snow in one storm, a U.S. record.

alts: Do people climb it to the top?
Can kids climb the big volcano?
z:735.a: Yes, climbers head for Mount Shasta's summit from late April into October.
z:735.quote: Climbers head for Mount Shasta's summit from late April into October.

z:735.q: What will we see around Mount Shasta?
alts: What can we see around it?
What's at the bottom of the big volcano?
z:735.a: The canyon opens onto the foot of the volcano. You'll see the city of Mount Shasta, the dark cone of Black Butte and Black Butte Summit.
z:735.quote: The canyon opens onto the foot of the volcano, with the city of Mount Shasta, the dark cone of Black Butte and Black Butte Summit.

z:746.q: Why did the town of Weed grow up here?
alts: Why did people build up Weed here?
Why is there even a town here, anyway?
z:746.a: Weed grew up around lumber mills. The lumber industry is what gave this town its start.
z:746.quote: Weed grew up around lumber mills.

z:746.q: What happened here when Shastina erupted?
alts: What did it do to the ground here?
What did the volcano do to this place, Mom?
z:746.a: Hot flows from Shastina's eruptions once covered the ground here. So the land around Weed was buried by those volcanic flows.
z:746.quote: Hot flows from Shastina's eruptions once covered the ground here

alts: Did stuff burn down here, Dad?
z:746.a: Yes. Recent wildfires have left their marks on the area around Weed, so you may notice signs of them along this stretch.
z:746.quote: recent wildfires have left their marks

alts: What happens at it in the summer?
Is there a party in Weed, Mom?
z:746.a: It's Weed's summer festival, with bocce ball tournaments. It's held each June or July.
z:746.quote: In summer: Weed holds its Carnevale, with bocce ball tournaments, each June or July.

z:756.q: What kind of valley is the Shasta Valley?
alts: What is it like out here?
What kind of place is this, Buddy?
z:756.a: It's a wide, dry valley sitting in the rain shadow of the Klamath Mountains. You'll see hay fields, cattle and juniper dotted across it.
z:756.quote: A wide, dry valley in the rain shadow of the Klamath Mountains, dotted with hummocks, with hay fields, cattle and juniper.

z:756.q: Does it rain in the Shasta Valley in summer?
alts: Does it rain here in summer?
Is it always sunny here, Buddy?
z:756.a: Almost never. Summer rain hardly ever falls here, except for an occasional thunderstorm.
z:756.quote: Summer rain almost never falls here, except for an occasional thunderstorm.

z:756.q: Does it snow in the Shasta Valley in winter?
alts: Is it cold here in winter, Buddy?
z:756.a: Yes, fairly often. Winters here are cool to cold, with fairly frequent snow.
z:756.quote: Winters are cool to cold, with fairly frequent snow.

z:770.q: What is Yreka gold country known for?
alts: Why is this place famous, mom?
z:770.a: This stretch is Gold Rush country, built around the county seat of Yreka. The Klamath Mountains rise to the west and the Shasta River cuts north toward the Klamath.
z:770.quote: Gold Rush country around the county seat, with the Klamath Mountains rising to the west and the Shasta River cutting north toward the Klamath.

z:770.q: What mountains are near Yreka gold country?
alts: What mountains are those over there?
Are there big mountains here, dad?
z:770.a: The Klamath Mountains rise to the west of this Gold Rush country around Yreka.
z:770.quote: Gold Rush country around the county seat, with the Klamath Mountains rising to the west

z:770.q: What river runs through Yreka gold country?
alts: What river is it near here?
Is there a river here, mom?
z:770.a: The Shasta River cuts north through this country toward the Klamath.
z:770.quote: the Shasta River cutting north toward the Klamath.

z:770.q: Is there a Gold Rush event in Yreka?
alts: Is there a fun gold thing to do, dad?
z:770.a: Yes, in summer Yreka holds Gold Rush Days every June.
z:770.quote: In summer: Yreka holds Gold Rush Days every June.

z:770.q: Does it snow much in Yreka?
alts: Does it snow a lot, mom?
z:770.a: Not much. Yreka averages only about 12 inches of snow a year, mostly from November through February.
z:770.quote: Yreka averages only about 12 inches of snow a year, mostly from November through February.

z:785.q: What are the Siskiyou Mountains north of the Klamath River?
alts: What are those mountains up ahead?
What are those big mountains, are they important?
z:785.a: The Siskiyou Mountains rise to the north. They're the divide between the Klamath and the Rogue.
z:785.quote: To the north rise the Siskiyou Mountains, the divide between the Klamath and the Rogue.

z:785.q: Does Siskiyou Summit get snow near the Oregon line?
alts: Will there be snow on the pass, can we play in it?
z:785.a: Yes. Just over the Oregon line, Siskiyou Summit usually gets snow from November through April.
z:785.quote: Just over the Oregon line, Siskiyou Summit usually gets snow from November through April.

z:785.q: What do people do with the land along the Klamath River here?
alts: What do they do with all this land?
Is somebody farming out here, what's growing?
z:785.a: The valley is farm and ranch country. Below the old Iron Gate Dam site, the Klamath runs through an arid valley of farms and ranches.
z:785.quote: the Klamath runs through an arid valley of farms and ranches.

mission-san-diego-de-alcala.q: When was Mission San Diego de Alcalá founded?
alts: When did they start this mission, like how long ago?
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.a: It was founded on July 16, 1769. It's the first of California's 21 missions.
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.quote: This is Mission San Diego de Alcalá, the first of California's 21 missions, founded on July 16, 1769.

mission-san-diego-de-alcala.q: Who founded Mission San Diego de Alcalá?
alts: Who made this place, like who was the boss?
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.a: Father Junípero Serra founded the mission in 1769, beside a new Spanish fort.
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.quote: Father Junípero Serra founded the mission in 1769 beside a new Spanish fort.

mission-san-diego-de-alcala.q: What happened to Mission San Diego de Alcalá in 1775?
alts: What happened to it back then?
Did something bad happen here, like a fight?
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.a: On November 4 and 5, 1775, people from several Kumeyaay villages surrounded the mission and burned it. Father Luis Jayme was killed.
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.quote: On November 4 and 5, 1775, people from several Kumeyaay villages surrounded the mission and burned it. Father Luis Jayme was killed.

mission-san-diego-de-alcala.q: Who are the Kumeyaay people connected to Mission San Diego de Alcalá?
alts: Who are the Kumeyaay, and what do they have to do with it?
Who lived here before the mission, like way back?
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.a: The Kumeyaay have lived in this valley for thousands of years, and they live in San Diego County today.
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.quote: The Kumeyaay have lived in this valley for thousands of years, and they live in San Diego County today.

mission-san-diego-de-alcala.q: What can we see at Mission San Diego de Alcalá?
alts: What's there to see at it?
Is there anything cool for kids to look at there?
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.a: Look for Father Jayme's tomb near the altar, a tall bell wall with five bells outside, and a small museum in the visitor center. The gardens are quiet.
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.quote: Inside the church, look for Father Jayme's tomb near the altar. Outside stands a tall bell wall with five bells.

mission-san-diego-de-alcala.q: Is the Mission San Diego de Alcalá church the original building?
alts: Is it really old or did they rebuild it?
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.a: Not quite. It's the fifth church on this site, largely rebuilt in 1931. Only one room, the Casa del Padre Serra, dates to 1774 and is believed to be the only original room.
mission-san-diego-de-alcala.quote: The church you see is the fifth on this site. It was largely rebuilt in 1931, following the design of the church dedicated in 1813.

alts: Who built this old mission, anyway?
mission-carmel.a: Father Junípero Serra founded it at Monterey in 1770 and moved it here in 1771. It was his headquarters until he died in 1784.
mission-carmel.quote: Father Junípero Serra founded it at Monterey in 1770 and moved it here in 1771. It was his headquarters until he died in 1784

mission-carmel.q: Why did Carmel Mission move from Monterey?
alts: Why did they pick up the mission and move it, Dad?
mission-carmel.a: Serra moved the mission here from Monterey, partly to keep Native people away from the soldiers.
mission-carmel.quote: Serra moved the mission here from Monterey, partly to keep Native people away from the soldiers.

mission-carmel.q: Is Father Serra buried at Carmel Mission?
alts: Is he buried in that church?
Is there a real grave in there?
mission-carmel.a: Yes. He died on August 28, 1784, and he is buried beneath the sanctuary floor of the church.
mission-carmel.quote: He is buried beneath the sanctuary floor.

mission-carmel.q: What is there to see at Carmel Mission?
alts: What can we see at it?
What cool stuff is in there?
mission-carmel.a: The stone church, four small museums, a chapel gallery, the cemetery and the gardens. Plan one to two hours. Easy to miss is Serra's simple cell in the convento museum.
mission-carmel.quote: Four small museums cover mission life, the Munras family and Serra's own simple cell in the convento.

mission-carmel.q: Is Carmel Mission still used today?
alts: Is it still a working church?
Do people still go to church there?
mission-carmel.a: Yes. It's an active Catholic parish and a minor basilica, so some areas close during Mass.
mission-carmel.quote: Today: Active Catholic parish and minor basilica of the Diocese of Monterey

mission-san-antonio-de-padua.q: What is Mission San Antonio de Padua known for?
alts: What's so special about this mission?
Why is it a big deal?
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.a: It was among the first places in Alta California to make fired red clay roof tiles, which protected buildings from fire.
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.quote: San Antonio was among the first places in Alta California to make fired red clay roof tiles, which protected buildings from fire.

mission-san-antonio-de-padua.q: Why is Mission San Antonio de Padua inside a military base?
alts: Why is it on an Army base?
Why is the mission inside a military base, Mom?
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.a: In World War Two the Army took over the surrounding ranch land, so the mission now sits inside a military base. The base has its own gate rules, so read the mission's directions page first.
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.quote: In World War Two the Army took over the surrounding ranch land, so the mission now sits inside a military base.

mission-san-antonio-de-padua.q: What is there to see at Mission San Antonio de Padua?
alts: What's there to do at the mission?
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.a: There's the rebuilt church, a museum with Native American and mission-era archaeology, and the original water system ruins beyond the church. There's also a gift shop and a retreat center.
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.quote: The museum holds Native American and mission-era archaeology and is the best stop for the Salinan story.

mission-san-antonio-de-padua.q: Whose homeland is Mission San Antonio de Padua on?
alts: Who lived here before the mission?
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.a: It sits in the homeland of the Salinan people, and the Salinan Tribe helps care for the cemetery here today. Salinan people did the farming and building at the mission.
mission-san-antonio-de-padua.quote: It sits in the homeland of the Salinan people, and the Salinan Tribe helps care for the cemetery here today.

mission-san-gabriel.q: When was Mission San Gabriel founded?
alts: When did they start this place, mom?
mission-san-gabriel.a: Mission San Gabriel was founded on September 8, 1771. It was later moved to its current spot a few years after, because of floods.
mission-san-gabriel.quote: founded on September 8, 1771 and moved here a few years later after floods

mission-san-gabriel.a: Fathers Pedro Benito Cambón and Ángel Fernández de la Somera founded it, under the authority of Junípero Serra. It was mission number 4 of 21.
mission-san-gabriel.quote: Fathers Pedro Benito Cambón and Ángel Fernández de la Somera founded the mission, under Serra's authority.

mission-san-gabriel.q: Who lived on this land before Mission San Gabriel?
alts: Whose land was it before that?
mission-san-gabriel.a: The mission stands in the homeland of the Tongva people. Some of their descendants use the name Kizh.
mission-san-gabriel.quote: It stands in the homeland of the Tongva people, and some of their descendants use the name Kizh.

mission-san-gabriel.q: What makes the church at Mission San Gabriel different from other missions?
alts: Why does that church look weird, dad?
mission-san-gabriel.a: Its architect, Father Antonio Cruzado, gave it tall narrow windows and capped buttresses. The California Missions Foundation ties that style to the cathedral of Córdoba in Spain.
mission-san-gabriel.quote: Its architect, Father Antonio Cruzado, gave it tall narrow windows and capped buttresses, a style the California Missions Foundation ties to the cathedral of Córdoba in Spain.

mission-san-gabriel.q: What happened to Mission San Gabriel in 2020?
alts: Did the church burn down, mom?
mission-san-gabriel.a: An arson fire destroyed the church roof on July 11, 2020. The roof was rebuilt, and the church walls are original from when it was finished in 1805.
mission-san-gabriel.quote: An arson fire destroyed the church roof on July 11, 2020.

mission-san-luis-obispo.q: Why was Mission San Luis Obispo built here?
alts: Why did they put it in this valley?
Why'd they pick this spot, anyway?
mission-san-luis-obispo.a: The soldiers and priests at Monterey were short of food in 1772. Serra sent hunters to this valley, and they brought back so much bear meat that he chose it for a mission.
mission-san-luis-obispo.quote: Serra sent a hunting party to this valley, and the hunters brought back so much bear meat that he chose it for a mission.

mission-san-luis-obispo.q: What is special about the church at Mission San Luis Obispo?
alts: What makes it different from the other missions?
Why is the church shaped funny?
mission-san-luis-obispo.a: Its church is the only L-shaped church among the California missions. A long second nave sits beside the main one, and that is what makes the L.
mission-san-luis-obispo.quote: The church is L-shaped, with a long second nave beside the main one.

mission-san-luis-obispo.q: Who built Mission San Luis Obispo?
mission-san-luis-obispo.a: Serra founded it on September 1, 1772, and Father José Cavaller built it with Chumash labor. It was the fifth mission.
mission-san-luis-obispo.quote: Father José Cavaller built it with Chumash labor.

mission-san-luis-obispo.q: Why does Mission San Luis Obispo have clay roof tiles?
alts: How did it start using tiles?
Why did they make tiles back then?
mission-san-luis-obispo.a: In 1776 a flaming arrow set the mission's thatched roofs on fire. The padres then began firing clay roof tiles here.
mission-san-luis-obispo.quote: In 1776 a flaming arrow set the mission's thatched roofs on fire. The padres then began firing clay roof tiles here.

mission-san-luis-obispo.q: Is Mission San Luis Obispo still used today?
alts: Is it still a working church?
Do people still go to church there?
Is it just a museum now?
mission-san-luis-obispo.a: Yes, it is still a working parish, Old Mission Parish. There is also a small museum and gift shop beside the church.
mission-san-luis-obispo.quote: The mission is still a working parish.

alts: How many years has that been standing?
mission-dolores.a: The first Mass here was said on June 29, 1776. The little adobe chapel was finished in 1791 and is the oldest intact building in San Francisco.
mission-dolores.quote: The first Mass here was said on June 29, 1776.

alts: Who built this place, like, way back?
mission-dolores.a: Father Francisco Palóu founded it with Father Pedro Benito Cambón. Serra was not there, though it was under his authority.
mission-dolores.quote: Father Francisco Palóu founded the mission with Father Pedro Benito Cambón. Serra was not there.

mission-dolores.q: Whose land is Mission Dolores on?
alts: Who lived here before it was built?
Who were the first people here?
mission-dolores.a: This is the homeland of the Ramaytush Ohlone, who are still here. People from the Yelamu group joined the mission, and Coast Miwok and others were brought from farther away.
mission-dolores.quote: This is the homeland of the Ramaytush Ohlone, who are still here.

mission-dolores.q: Did Mission Dolores survive the 1906 earthquake?
alts: Did the big shaking knock it down?
mission-dolores.a: The original adobe chapel did survive. The brick church built next door in 1876 did not make it through 1906.
mission-dolores.quote: The adobe chapel is original, finished in 1791, and it survived the 1906 earthquake.

mission-dolores.q: What is there to see at Mission Dolores?
alts: What can we see at it?
Is there cool stuff to look at?
mission-dolores.a: You can see the original adobe chapel, whose ceiling still shows Ohlone designs in plant dyes, plus a small museum and the cemetery. Plan 45 minutes to an hour.
mission-dolores.quote: The ceiling still shows Ohlone designs painted in plant dyes.

mission-san-juan-capistrano.q: What is Mission San Juan Capistrano famous for?
alts: Why is this place so famous, mom?
mission-san-juan-capistrano.a: It is famous for its swallows. The Serra Chapel there is also regarded as the oldest building in California still in use.
mission-san-juan-capistrano.quote: The mission is famous for its swallows.

mission-san-juan-capistrano.q: When was Mission San Juan Capistrano founded?
alts: How old is this place, dad?
mission-san-juan-capistrano.a: It was founded on November 1, 1776, after a first try in 1775 was abandoned within days.
mission-san-juan-capistrano.quote: founded on November 1, 1776, after a first try in 1775 was abandoned within days.

mission-san-juan-capistrano.q: Why did the priests abandon the first attempt at the mission?
alts: Why did they leave it at first?
Why did the priests run away and bury the bells?
mission-san-juan-capistrano.a: Word came that Kumeyaay people had burned Mission San Diego, so the priests buried the bells and left. Serra later returned and founded the mission on All Saints' Day, 1776.
mission-san-juan-capistrano.quote: When word came that Kumeyaay people had burned Mission San Diego, the priests buried the bells and left.

mission-san-juan-capistrano.q: What happened to the Great Stone Church?
alts: Why is the big church just ruins?
mission-san-juan-capistrano.a: It collapsed in the earthquake of December 8, 1812, during Mass, and about 40 people died. The ruins still stand today, kept as ruins.
mission-san-juan-capistrano.quote: It collapsed in the earthquake of December 8, 1812, during Mass, and about 40 people died.

mission-san-juan-capistrano.q: Who lived here before the mission was built?
alts: Who lived on this land first?
Were there Native people here before the mission?
mission-san-juan-capistrano.a: This is Acjachemen homeland. They lived in villages along the creeks here, and Acjachemen families still live in this region and keep their language and traditions alive.
mission-san-juan-capistrano.quote: The Acjachemen lived in villages along these creeks, and the large village of Putuidem lay about a mile north.

mission-santa-clara.q: When was Mission Santa Clara founded?
alts: How long ago did they start this place, mom?
mission-santa-clara.a: Mission Santa Clara was founded on January 12, 1777. It was the eighth of the 21 California missions, and the first one named for a woman.
mission-santa-clara.quote: This is Mission Santa Clara, founded on January 12, 1777, the first California mission named for a woman.

mission-santa-clara.q: Is the Mission Santa Clara church the original building?
alts: Is that the real old church?
Did they build this a really long time ago, dad?
mission-santa-clara.a: No, it's a replica. A fire in October 1926 destroyed the church, and it was rebuilt in concrete in 1928 and 1929 with one bell tower like the 1825 church.
mission-santa-clara.quote: A fire in October 1926 destroyed the church, which had been enlarged and given a wooden front in the 1800s.

mission-santa-clara.q: What is special about Mission Santa Clara compared to other missions?
alts: Why is this mission cool, dad?
mission-santa-clara.a: It's the only mission on a university campus. It stands on the grounds of Santa Clara University, which the Jesuits opened as a college in 1851.
mission-santa-clara.quote: This is the only mission on a university campus.

mission-santa-clara.q: Who lived here before Mission Santa Clara was built?
alts: Whose land was it before that?
Did people live here first, mom?
mission-santa-clara.a: This is the homeland of the Tamien Ohlone. The first Mass was said at their village of So-co-is-u-ka on the Guadalupe River.
mission-santa-clara.quote: Father Tomás de la Peña said the first Mass at the Tamien village of So-co-is-u-ka on the Guadalupe River.

mission-santa-clara.q: What can we see at Mission Santa Clara?
alts: What's there to do at it?
Is there anything fun to see, mom?
mission-santa-clara.a: You can visit the church, with a bell tower holding bells cast in different years. You can also walk the quiet mission gardens, easy to miss among the campus paths.
mission-santa-clara.quote: Easy to miss: the mission gardens, tucked among the campus paths. The church is open to visitors.

mission-santa-clara.q: Is Mission Santa Clara still used today?
alts: Is it a real church now, dad?
mission-santa-clara.a: Yes, it's a working chapel on the Santa Clara University campus. Some hours are set aside for services, so check before you go.
mission-santa-clara.quote: It is also a working chapel, so some hours are set aside for services. Check before you go.

mission-san-buenaventura.a: Junípero Serra founded it. It was the last mission he founded, back in 1782.
mission-san-buenaventura.quote: This is Mission San Buenaventura in Ventura, founded by Serra on Easter Sunday, March 31, 1782. It was the last mission he founded.

mission-san-buenaventura.q: When was Mission San Buenaventura founded?
alts: How many years ago was this built, Mom?
mission-san-buenaventura.a: It was founded on Easter Sunday, March 31, 1782. It was the ninth of the 21 California missions.
mission-san-buenaventura.quote: founded by Serra on Easter Sunday, March 31, 1782.

mission-san-buenaventura.q: What can we see at Mission San Buenaventura?
alts: What is there to see at it?
mission-san-buenaventura.a: The museum has two wooden bells, the only wooden bells known from any California mission. There's also a thirty-minute history video and a garden with a grotto.
mission-san-buenaventura.quote: A small museum holds two wooden bells, the only wooden bells known from any California mission.

mission-san-buenaventura.q: What are the wooden bells at Mission San Buenaventura for?
alts: Why does it have wooden bells?
Why are the bells made of wood, Mom?
mission-san-buenaventura.a: They were rung during Holy Week, when the metal bells were silent. They're the only wooden bells known from any California mission.
mission-san-buenaventura.quote: They were rung during Holy Week, when the metal bells were silent.

mission-san-buenaventura.q: Is Mission San Buenaventura still used today?
alts: Do people still go there, Dad?
mission-san-buenaventura.a: Yes, it's a living parish and a minor basilica, with a museum too. Be quiet if there's a Mass going on.
mission-san-buenaventura.quote: The mission is a living parish, so be quiet during Mass.

mission-san-buenaventura.q: What happened at Mission San Buenaventura in 1812?
alts: What happened to it back then?
Did something bad happen here, Mom?
mission-san-buenaventura.a: Earthquakes in 1812 and a wave from the sea sent the friars and Chumash people inland for a time.
mission-san-buenaventura.quote: The earthquakes of 1812 and a wave from the sea sent the friars and Chumash people inland for a time.

mission-santa-barbara.q: Who founded Old Mission Santa Barbara?
alts: Who built the mission, kids want to know?
mission-santa-barbara.a: Father Fermín Lasuén founded it on December 4, 1786, on the feast of Saint Barbara. It was the tenth of the 21 missions.
mission-santa-barbara.quote: Father Fermín Lasuén founded the mission on the feast of Saint Barbara.

mission-santa-barbara.q: What can we see and do at Old Mission Santa Barbara?
alts: What's there to see at it?
What's cool to look at there for kids?
mission-santa-barbara.a: There's a nine-room museum, fifteen acres of gardens, the original fountain, and the lavadero, a stone basin where women washed clothes. An audio tour comes in six languages.
mission-santa-barbara.quote: The museum fills nine rooms, and the gardens cover fifteen acres.

mission-santa-barbara.q: Is the church at Old Mission Santa Barbara the original building?
alts: Is that church the original one?
Did the mission fall down in an earthquake?
mission-santa-barbara.a: No. An 1812 earthquake destroyed the third church. The stone church you see was built from about 1815 to 1820, and a 1925 earthquake caused extensive damage, with repairs finished in 1927.
mission-santa-barbara.quote: The earthquake of December 21, 1812 destroyed the third church. The stone church you see was built from about 1815 to 1820.

mission-santa-barbara.q: Who are the Chumash people connected to Old Mission Santa Barbara?
alts: Who were the Chumash at that mission?
Who lived there before the mission?
mission-santa-barbara.a: This is Chumash homeland, and Barbareño Chumash people are still here. Today the mission offers space for classes in the Barbareño Chumash language.
mission-santa-barbara.quote: This is Chumash homeland, and Barbareño Chumash people are still here.

mission-la-purisima.q: When was La Purísima Mission founded?
alts: When did they build this place, mom?
mission-la-purisima.a: La Purísima Mission was founded on December 8, 1787. It was the 11th of the 21 California missions in founding order.
mission-la-purisima.quote: This is La Purísima Mission, founded on December 8, 1787.

mission-la-purisima.a: Father Fermín Lasuén founded it, at a Chumash place called Algsacpi, near today's downtown Lompoc.
mission-la-purisima.quote: Father Fermín Lasuén founded the mission at a Chumash place called Algsacpi, near today's downtown Lompoc.

mission-la-purisima.q: Why was La Purísima Mission moved to a new site?
alts: What happened to the first mission?
Did something bad happen to it, mom?
mission-la-purisima.a: An earthquake and heavy rains on December 21, 1812 destroyed the buildings. The mission was re-founded at this new site on April 23, 1813.
mission-la-purisima.quote: The earthquake and heavy rains of December 21, 1812 destroyed the buildings. The mission was re-founded on April 23, 1813 at this new site.

mission-la-purisima.q: Are the buildings at La Purísima Mission original?
alts: Did they fake the old stuff, dad?
mission-la-purisima.a: No, it's a reconstruction. Civilian Conservation Corps crews built it from the ruins between 1934 and 1941, so the walls are not original.
mission-la-purisima.quote: It is a reconstruction, built from ruins by Civilian Conservation Corps crews from 1934 to 1941, so the walls are not original.

mission-la-purisima.q: What can we see and do at La Purísima Mission?
mission-la-purisima.a: You can see the church, the padre's chapel and ten restored buildings, plus a five-acre garden. The corrals hold burros, horses, longhorn cattle, sheep and goats, and there are trails and horseback rides.
mission-la-purisima.quote: There is a five-acre garden, and the corrals hold burros, horses, longhorn cattle, sheep and goats.

mission-la-purisima.q: Is La Purísima Mission still a church today?
mission-la-purisima.a: No, it is not a parish church. Today it is a state historic park run by California State Parks, so you can wander at your own pace.
mission-la-purisima.quote: Today it is a state historic park, and Chumash people still live in this region.

mission-santa-cruz.q: How old is Mission Santa Cruz?
alts: How many years ago did they build this thing?
mission-santa-cruz.a: Mission Santa Cruz was founded on August 28, 1791, when Father Fermín Lasuén raised the cross. It was the twelfth of the 21 California missions.
mission-santa-cruz.quote: Father Fermín Lasuén raised the cross on August 28, 1791.

mission-santa-cruz.q: Why is it called Mission Santa Cruz?
alts: Why's it called Santa Cruz, like what's it mean?
mission-santa-cruz.a: It is named for the Holy Cross, and it is the only mission with that name.
mission-santa-cruz.quote: founded on August 28, 1791, the only mission named for the Holy Cross.

mission-santa-cruz.q: Is anything original left at Mission Santa Cruz?
alts: Is any of it still original?
Is any of the real old stuff still here?
mission-santa-cruz.a: Just one original building survives, an adobe built from 1822 to 1824 for Native Yokuts and Ohlone families. The chapel on High Street is a replica finished in 1931.
mission-santa-cruz.quote: Only one original building survives, an adobe that housed Native families.

mission-santa-cruz.q: Who lived here before Mission Santa Cruz was built?
alts: Whose land was it before that?
Who were the Native people here, before the mission?
mission-santa-cruz.a: This is the homeland of the Awaswas-speaking Ohlone, the Uypi people. Yokuts families also lived at the mission.
mission-santa-cruz.quote: This is the homeland of the Awaswas-speaking Ohlone, the Uypi people.

mission-santa-cruz.q: Why is it called the hard-luck mission?
alts: What bad stuff happened to it, like floods and earthquakes?
mission-santa-cruz.a: Floods soon forced the mission up to Mission Hill, and the 1857 earthquake knocked down the front wall of the old church. That's how it earned the nickname.
mission-santa-cruz.quote: The mission was nicknamed the hard-luck mission for its floods and quakes.

mission-soledad.q: Why is it called Mission Soledad?
alts: Why does it have that weird name, Soledad?
mission-soledad.a: Soledad means solitude. The full Spanish name is Misión Nuestra Señora de la Soledad.

mission-soledad.q: When was Mission Soledad founded, and by whom?
alts: How old is it and who started it?
Who built this old mission, and when?
mission-soledad.a: It was founded on October 9, 1791 in the Salinas Valley by Father Fermín Lasuén. It was the 13th of the 21 missions.
mission-soledad.quote: This is Mission Soledad, founded on October 9, 1791 in the Salinas Valley.

mission-soledad.q: Is the chapel at Mission Soledad the original one?
alts: Is that chapel the real old one?
Is the old building really old, or is it fake?
mission-soledad.a: No, the small chapel was rebuilt in the 1950s. The long adobe ruins beside it are original, the unrestored walls of the old quadrangle.
mission-soledad.quote: The small chapel you enter is a rebuild from the 1950s, so it is not original.

mission-soledad.q: What happened to Mission Soledad after the mission era?
alts: What happened to it after the missions ended?
Why did the mission fall apart?
mission-soledad.a: After Mexico ended the mission system, it was sold for a reported 800 dollars, stripped for building materials and left in ruins. The chapel was rebuilt and dedicated in 1955.
mission-soledad.quote: After Mexico ended the mission system, the mission was sold for a reported 800 dollars, stripped for building materials and left in ruins.

mission-soledad.q: Who lived here before Mission Soledad was built?
alts: Who were the Native people of this land?
Were there Native Americans here before it?
mission-soledad.a: Esselen and Chalon Ohlone people lived in this valley, and the mission was founded near an Esselen village. Yokuts and Salinan people were brought here later.
mission-soledad.quote: Father FermÃ­n LasuÃ©n founded the mission near an Esselen village.

mission-san-jose.q: Is Mission San José in the city of San Jose?
alts: Wait, is this the San Jose from the map?
mission-san-jose.a: No. Mission San José is in Fremont, not in the city of San Jose.
mission-san-jose.quote: This is Mission San José in Fremont, founded on June 11, 1797 at the Ohlone village of Oroysom. It is not in the city of San Jose.

mission-san-jose.q: Is the church at Mission San José the original building?
alts: Is it the real old church?
Is that church really old, or new?
mission-san-jose.a: No, the church you see is a replica, built from 1982 to 1985. It copies the 1809 adobe church, which the 1868 Hayward Fault earthquake shattered.
mission-san-jose.quote: The church is a replica of the 1809 adobe church. The Hayward Fault earthquake of October 21, 1868 shattered the original, and the replica was built from 1982 to 1985.

mission-san-jose.q: Who founded Mission San José and when?
alts: Who started it and when was it founded?
Who built this place, and how long ago?
mission-san-jose.a: Father Fermín Lasuén founded it on June 11, 1797, at the Ohlone village of Oroysom. Native people from Mission Santa Clara did the first building.
mission-san-jose.quote: Father Fermín Lasuén founded the mission. Native people from Mission Santa Clara did the first building.

mission-san-jose.q: What is there to see at Mission San José?
alts: What can we see inside it?
What's cool to look at there?
mission-san-jose.a: Look for the original hammered copper baptismal font and the bell wheel the Ohlone used during the sacred parts of Mass. The museum is in an original adobe wing, one of the few old buildings left.
mission-san-jose.quote: the original hammered copper baptismal font has been returned, along with the bell wheel the Ohlone used during the sacred parts of Mass.

mission-san-juan-bautista.q: How old is Mission San Juan Bautista?
alts: Mom, how long ago was this place built?
mission-san-juan-bautista.a: It was founded on June 24, 1797, so it has stood for a very long time. It was the fifteenth of the 21 California missions founded.
mission-san-juan-bautista.quote: This is Mission San Juan Bautista, founded on June 24, 1797, and nicknamed the Mission of Music.

mission-san-juan-bautista.q: Why is Mission San Juan Bautista called the Mission of Music?
alts: Why do they call it that?
Why is it the music mission?
mission-san-juan-bautista.a: Father Estevan Tapis taught a Native boys' choir using color-coded music notation. That choir earned the mission its nickname, the Mission of Music.
mission-san-juan-bautista.quote: Father Estevan Tapis taught a Native boys' choir with color-coded music notation, which earned the mission its nickname.

mission-san-juan-bautista.q: What is special about the church at Mission San Juan Bautista?
alts: Why is the church different from the other missions?
mission-san-juan-bautista.a: Its church is the only one among the California missions with three aisles. The side aisles were walled in after earthquake damage and reopened in 1975.
mission-san-juan-bautista.quote: Its church is the only one among the California missions with three aisles.

mission-san-juan-bautista.q: Is Mission San Juan Bautista really on the San Andreas Fault?
alts: Is it really on top of that earthquake fault?
Can we see where the earthquake fault is?
mission-san-juan-bautista.a: Yes. The fault runs just below the cemetery wall, and the 1906 earthquake ruined the outer walls. Earthquake damage in 1812 also led to the side aisles being walled in.
mission-san-juan-bautista.quote: The San Andreas Fault runs just below the cemetery wall, and the earthquake of 1906 ruined the outer walls.

mission-san-juan-bautista.q: What movie was filmed at Mission San Juan Bautista?
alts: Mom, did a famous movie use this place?
mission-san-juan-bautista.a: It appeared in Alfred Hitchcock's 1958 film Vertigo. The studio added the bell tower you see in the movie.
mission-san-juan-bautista.quote: The mission appeared in Alfred Hitchcock's 1958 film Vertigo, and the studio added the bell tower you see in the movie.

mission-san-miguel.q: When was Mission San Miguel founded?
alts: When did they start this place, like how long ago?
mission-san-miguel.a: Mission San Miguel was founded on July 25, 1797, in Salinan homeland. The church you see today was finished in 1818.
mission-san-miguel.quote: This is Mission San Miguel, founded on July 25, 1797, in Salinan homeland. Its church, finished in 1818

mission-san-miguel.q: Why was Mission San Miguel built where it is?
alts: Why did they put it there?
Why did they build it here, who picked this spot?
mission-san-miguel.a: Father Fermín Lasuén founded it to close the gap between San Antonio and San Luis Obispo. The site was chosen because many Salinan people lived nearby, close to a village called Vahca.
mission-san-miguel.quote: Father Fermín Lasuén founded the mission to close the gap between San Antonio and San Luis Obispo.

mission-san-miguel.q: What is Mission San Miguel famous for?
alts: What's the big deal about it, why do people stop?
mission-san-miguel.a: Its church still has the original painted walls, which have never been repainted. It's the place to see what a mission church really looked like inside.
mission-san-miguel.quote: This is the place to see what a mission church really looked like inside.

mission-san-miguel.q: Who painted the walls inside Mission San Miguel?
alts: Who made the pictures on the walls in it?
Who did the colorful painting, was it kids or grownups?
mission-san-miguel.a: The bright interior was painted by Native people under the supervision of Esteban Munras, a Spanish artist. The painted patterns are the work of Native artists.
mission-san-miguel.quote: its bright interior was painted by Native people under the supervision of Esteban Munras, a Spanish artist.

mission-san-miguel.q: What happened to Mission San Miguel in the 2003 earthquake?
alts: Did the whole church fall down in the earthquake?
mission-san-miguel.a: The San Simeon earthquake of December 22, 2003 severely damaged the church and closed it for six years. It was repaired and reopened in 2009.
mission-san-miguel.quote: The San Simeon earthquake of December 22, 2003 closed the church for six years, and it reopened in 2009.

mission-san-miguel.q: Is Mission San Miguel still used as a church today?
alts: Do people still go to church there?
Is anybody still in it, like does anyone still pray there?
mission-san-miguel.a: Yes, it's an active Catholic parish of the Diocese of Monterey, with a museum. It's a working parish, so be quiet during Mass.
mission-san-miguel.quote: This is a working parish, so be quiet during Mass.

mission-san-fernando.q: How old is Mission San Fernando?
alts: How long ago did they start this mission, Dad?
mission-san-fernando.a: Mission San Fernando was founded on September 8, 1797. It was the 17th of the 21 California missions, in founding order.
mission-san-fernando.quote: This is Mission San Fernando, founded on September 8, 1797, at the settlement of Achooykomenga.

mission-san-fernando.a: Father Fermín Lasuén founded it, on a farming settlement called Achooykomenga. The land was worked by Ventureño Chumash, Tongva and Tataviam laborers.
mission-san-fernando.quote: Father Fermín Lasuén founded the mission on a farming settlement called Achooykomenga, worked by Ventureño Chumash, Tongva and Tataviam laborers.

mission-san-fernando.q: Why is it called San Fernando, like the valley?
alts: Is that where the valley's name comes from?
Why does the valley have the same name, Mom?
mission-san-fernando.a: It works the other way around. The mission gave its name to the San Fernando Valley.
mission-san-fernando.quote: The mission gave its name to the San Fernando Valley.

mission-san-fernando.q: Is the church at Mission San Fernando original?
alts: Is it the real old church?
Did the church fall down, Dad?
mission-san-fernando.a: No. The 1971 San Fernando earthquake destroyed the church, and it was rebuilt by 1974. The long convento next to it is original and was finished in 1822.
mission-san-fernando.quote: The church beside it is not original. The 1971 San Fernando earthquake destroyed it and it was rebuilt by 1974

mission-san-fernando.q: What can we see at Mission San Fernando?
alts: What is there to do at it?
Is there anything cool to see, Mom?
mission-san-fernando.a: You can see the long convento with its nineteen-arch colonnade, the church, and a courtyard fountain described as original. Bob Hope and his wife Dolores are buried in the memorial garden.
mission-san-fernando.quote: Bob Hope and his wife Dolores are buried in the memorial garden.

mission-san-luis-rey.q: When was Mission San Luis Rey founded and by whom?
alts: When did they build it and who started it?
Who made this mission, and how long ago?
mission-san-luis-rey.a: It was founded on June 13, 1798, by Father Fermín Lasuén. It was mission number 18 of the 21 missions, in founding order.
mission-san-luis-rey.quote: This is Mission San Luis Rey, nicknamed the King of the Missions, founded on June 13, 1798.

mission-san-luis-rey.q: What is special about the church at Mission San Luis Rey?
alts: What makes that church different from the others?
Is there anything cool about the church?
mission-san-luis-rey.a: It was finished in 1815 and is the only surviving mission church built in the shape of a cross. It has a wooden dome and cupola.
mission-san-luis-rey.quote: The church finished in 1815 is the only surviving mission church built in the shape of a cross.

mission-san-luis-rey.q: Who was Pablo Tac at Mission San Luis Rey?
alts: Who was that boy who went to Rome?
Was there a famous kid from here?
mission-san-luis-rey.a: He was born at the mission around 1822. A priest took him to Rome as a boy, and there he wrote down the Luiseño language and the story of his people.
mission-san-luis-rey.quote: Pablo Tac was born here around 1822. A priest took him to Rome as a boy

mission-san-luis-rey.q: What is there to see at Mission San Luis Rey?
alts: What can we see when we stop at it?
What is there to look at, is it fun?
mission-san-luis-rey.a: Besides the church, the grounds have soldiers' barracks, the lavandería where clothes were washed, a kiln, a museum, the Madonna Chapel, and the first pepper tree planted in California, in 1830.
mission-san-luis-rey.quote: the quadrangle holds the soldiers' barracks, the lavandería where clothes were washed, a kiln and the first pepper tree planted in California, in 1830.

mission-santa-ines.q: When was Mission Santa Inés founded?
alts: When did they build this place, mom?
mission-santa-ines.a: Mission Santa Inés was founded on September 17, 1804, by Father Estevan Tapis. It is mission number 19 of the 21 California missions.
mission-santa-ines.quote: This is Mission Santa Inés in Solvang, founded on September 17, 1804.

mission-santa-ines.q: What happened at Mission Santa Inés in 1824?
alts: What happened here with the revolt?
Did something bad happen here, dad?
mission-santa-ines.a: On February 21, 1824, a soldier beat a young Chumash man here, and people rose up. The revolt spread to La Purísima and Santa Barbara, and Chumash people burned parts of this mission.
mission-santa-ines.quote: On February 21, 1824, a soldier beat a young Chumash man here, and people rose up.

mission-santa-ines.q: What can we see at Mission Santa Inés?
alts: What is there to do at it?
Is there anything cool inside, dad?
mission-santa-ines.a: The museum holds vestments, art, old manuscripts and bells. The mission garden and the rose garden are good places to sit, and there is a gift shop on site.
mission-santa-ines.quote: The museum holds vestments, art, old manuscripts and bells. The mission garden and the rose garden are good places to sit.

mission-santa-ines.q: Is the church at Mission Santa Inés the original one?
alts: Is it the same church from way back?
Is this the real old church, mom?
mission-santa-ines.a: The first church was mostly destroyed by the earthquake of December 21, 1812. The present church was dedicated on July 4, 1817, and its walls are original.
mission-santa-ines.quote: The earthquake of December 21, 1812 destroyed most of the first church, and the present church was dedicated on July 4, 1817.

mission-santa-ines.q: Is Mission Santa Inés still used today?
alts: Do people still go to it?
Does anyone still live there, mom?
mission-santa-ines.a: Yes. It is an active Catholic parish of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, served by Capuchin Franciscan friars since 1924, and it also has a museum.
mission-santa-ines.quote: Active Catholic parish of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, served by Capuchin Franciscan friars since 1924; museum

mission-san-rafael.q: Why was Mission San Rafael built?
alts: Why'd they make a mission here, Dad?
mission-san-rafael.a: It was founded in 1817 as a hospital outpost of Mission Dolores for sick Native people. It was meant to heal people who were sick in foggy San Francisco.
mission-san-rafael.quote: It was meant to heal Native people who were sick in foggy San Francisco, and it is called Alta California's first sanitarium.

mission-san-rafael.a: Father Vicente Francisco de Sarría founded it on December 14, 1817, as an asistencia of Mission Dolores.
mission-san-rafael.quote: Father Vicente Francisco de Sarría founded San Rafael as an asistencia of Mission Dolores.

mission-san-rafael.q: Why is it called Mission San Rafael?
alts: Why's it got that name, Dad?
mission-san-rafael.a: It was named for the archangel of healing, which fits its purpose as a place to heal sick people.
mission-san-rafael.quote: It was named for the archangel of healing.

mission-san-rafael.q: Is the Mission San Rafael building original?
alts: Is it the real old building?
Is this the real one, Mom?
mission-san-rafael.a: No. The ruins were cleared away by 1870. The chapel you see is a replica built in 1949 near the site of the original hospital.
mission-san-rafael.quote: No original buildings survive here, since the ruins were cleared away by 1870.

mission-san-rafael.q: What can we see at Mission San Rafael?
alts: What's there to see at it?
Is there anything cool to look at, Dad?
mission-san-rafael.a: There's the replica chapel with its star-shaped window, plus a small museum showing three of the four original mission bells. Plan 30 to 45 minutes.
mission-san-rafael.quote: A small museum and gift shop sit on the grounds, and the museum shows three of the four original mission bells.

alts: How long ago did they build this mission?
mission-sonoma.a: Sonoma Mission was founded on July 4, 1823. It was the last of the 21 missions, and the northernmost one.
mission-sonoma.quote: This is Sonoma Mission, the last and northernmost of the 21 missions, founded on July 4, 1823.

alts: Who was the guy who built this place?
mission-sonoma.a: Father José Altimira founded it, with soldiers and Native people who were moved over from Mission Dolores.
mission-sonoma.quote: Father José Altimira founded the mission, with soldiers and Native people moved from Mission Dolores.

mission-sonoma.q: What makes Sonoma Mission different from the other missions?
alts: Why is it the last one?
What's the deal with that mission?
mission-sonoma.a: It is the only mission founded after Mexico won independence from Spain. It was also the last and northernmost of the 21.
mission-sonoma.quote: It is the only one founded after Mexico won independence from Spain.

mission-sonoma.q: What happened at Sonoma Mission in 1826?
alts: Did something bad happen to it?
mission-sonoma.a: Native people who lived outside the mission were unhappy about their share of the harvest and burned some of the wooden buildings. Altimira fled.
mission-sonoma.quote: In 1826 Native people who lived outside the mission were unhappy about their share of the harvest and burned some of the wooden buildings. Altimira fled.

mission-sonoma.q: What can we see at Sonoma Mission?
alts: Is it worth stopping at it?
Is there anything cool to look at?
mission-sonoma.a: The museum shows paintings by Chris Jorgensen, and outside is the Sonoma Mission Indian Memorial. The same park has the Sonoma Barracks and Vallejo's home.
mission-sonoma.quote: Inside, the museum shows the paintings of Chris Jorgensen, who painted the California missions. Outside stands the Sonoma Mission Indian Memorial

mission-sonoma.q: Is Sonoma Mission still a church today?
alts: Is it a church or a museum?
mission-sonoma.a: No, it is a museum, not a church. It is part of Sonoma State Historic Park.
mission-sonoma.quote: This is a museum, not a church.
